5daf583aba2b3f03: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Peak electricity demand from the data centre industry in Peninsular Malaysia is projected to reach 8.39 gigawatts (GW) by 2030, based on the current electricity supply planning estimates, according to the Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation (Petra).
Of the total amount, Johor is expected to record the highest demand for electricity at 4.42GW, and Selangor at 1.48GW.

“Both states are major hubs for data centre development and will therefore require proper electricity supply infrastructure planning that takes into account the anticipated growth in demand,” it said.

The ministry was responding to a question from Onn Abu Bakar (PH-Batu Pahat) on the projected electricity and water demand by the data centre industry up to 2030, particularly in Johor and Selangor, as well as the number of data centres that have been completed.
Petra said 45 data centres had been completed and were operational in Peninsular Malaysia as of August 2026, with a combined electricity supply capacity of 6.04GW.
This capacity refers to the electricity supply provided by Tenaga Nasional Bhd through the National Grid to support the operation of the data centres.
Meanwhile, the projected water demand from data centres in Selangor and Johor is expected to reach 389.04 million litres per day (MLD) by 2030.
“However, actual water consumption by data centres currently reported to the National Water Services Commission stands at 63.90 MLD,” Petra said. — Bernama
cd7df366e1b10288: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Lumut Naval Shipyard Sdn Bhd (Lunas) remains committed to delivering the first littoral combat ship (LCS1) to the Royal Malaysian Navy (RMN), with the target for physical delivery revised to April 2027.

Lunas said the revised delivery timeline for LCS1 should be viewed in the context of the programme’s overall technical, regulatory and contractual complexities, and the ship’s delivery schedule was affected by the cancellation of the export licence for the surface-to-surface missile system by the Norwegian authorities as well.

Following the decision, Lunas was no longer permitted under international export control regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), to deliver a ship equipped with the missile launcher system in question.

Lunas said it had formally informed the Defence Ministry (Mindef) of the technical, cost and scheduling implications arising from the development, which fell outside the scope and control of the company’s original contract.

The company also explained that several critical complementary contracts required for physical delivery were not included in Lunas’ existing scope and had to be contracted directly by Mindef with the original equipment manufacturers.
In addition, the Letter of Acceptance (LoA) for the Integrated Logistics Support and Test Assistance package was issued in August 2025, but the contract was only finalised and signed in August 2026.
Lunas said the delay had affected the implementation of the training programme, which formed an important part of the package’s scope.

On the proposed imposition of Liquidated and Ascertained Damages (LAD), Lunas said any determination of contractual responsibility must be made through the prescribed contractual and legal mechanisms, and that the Auditor-General’s Report should not be regarded as a final determination of contractual liability.
The company said the audit was conducted based on information provided by Mindef and the RMN, while respecting the report’s findings and recommendations.

Lunas reaffirmed its commitment to delivering an LCS that is safe, capable and mission-ready to strengthen the RMN’s operational readiness. However, the target for physical delivery in April 2027 could be pushed back further if the Contract Variation Order continued to be delayed. — Bernama
21898fe4bc5238a4: BENGALURU: National Australia Bank Ltd (NAB) will cut up to 2,500 jobs, or about six per cent of its workforce, over the next year to simplify operations and reduce costs amid pressure on Australia's credit growth.
The bank, Australia's biggest business lender and third-largest home lender, said up to 1,500 positions would be cut by the end of 2026.
The largest cuts will target corporate roles rather than customer-facing bankers, while the bank also plans to materially reduce its reliance on consultants and contractors.
"Our ambition and strategy remain unchanged. We will improve productivity, risk outcomes and execution to be a simpler and more efficient bank," chief executive Andrew Irvine said in a statement.
NAB shares fell nearly 2.5 per cent on Tuesday, recording the biggest decline among Australia's four major retail banks. The S&P/ASX 200 index was down 0.9 per cent.
NAB said it would begin consultations with the Finance Sector Union, whose national assistant secretary Nicole McPherson said the job cuts would not help simplify the organisation.

"To take a wrecking ball to 6% of one of Australia's largest workforces this close to Christmas is disgraceful and shows that NAB's leadership is completely detached from the lived experience of their workers," she said.
The restructuring will incur a pre-tax charge of about A$300 million (US$209 million) in 2027, covering redundancy, redeployment and organisational redesign costs.
This compares with pre-tax charges of about A$80 million in each of 2025 and 2026, NAB said.
The job cuts come as Australia's banks face mounting pressure from weaker housing activity, intensifying competition and higher operating costs, which are weighing on earnings.

In August, NAB warned that housing credit growth would slow sharply in 2027 following the federal government's property tax reforms, which the bank said had dampened demand from homebuyers and investors.
At the time, Irvine said geopolitical uncertainty, higher domestic interest rates and tax changes were creating challenges for customers.
NAB employed 41,880 people globally as at Sept 30, 2025, according to its latest annual report.

The move follows a similar restructuring drive by rival ANZ, which last year announced plans to cut about 3,500 jobs by September 2026 under chief executive Nuno Matos as part of a programme to simplify operations, reduce duplication and lower costs.
148ed9b6905e497f: PETALING JAYA: The public should not assume that every infrastructure problem is the responsibility of one party alone, as jurisdiction, implementation and funding may involve both the federal and state governments.
Universiti Malaysia Sabah lecturer Ramli Dollah explained that the division of responsibilities between the federal and state governments is broadly set out in the Federal Constitution.
He said the federal list, state list and concurrent list contained in the ninth schedule to the constitution outlines the powers and jurisdiction of each level of government.
“The people must be careful not to immediately assume that all infrastructure problems are the responsibility of (the federal) government.
“We must distinguish between three things: who has jurisdiction, who implements the project, and who provides the money. Sometimes these three things involve different governments,” he told FMT.
In general, areas such as defence, internal security, education, and medicine and health fall under the federal government.
The states, meanwhile, are responsible for land, agriculture, forestry and local government, while both levels manage social welfare, town and country planning, and certain aspects of public health.
As a result, Ramli said problems cannot automatically be attributed to the federal or state governments simply because of where they occur.
For example, land and forestry are state matters, meaning issues related to forest management and timber resources should be viewed based on the responsibilities of the state government concerned.
Despite this, the federal government also channels various forms of grants to states to help finance their responsibilities and support development.
In March, the National Finance Council agreed to improve federal grants to states—with allocations projected to reach RM10.5 billion this year, compared with RM10.3 billion in 2025.
These include allocations for matters contained in the concurrent list, state road maintenance, and the distribution of tourism tax revenue.
Roads and water supply
Roads are one of the clearest examples of how responsibilities are divided between federal and state.
Federal roads are under the responsibility of the federal government, while state roads are managed by state governments. Some roads also fall within the jurisdiction of local authorities.

However, that does not mean all costs incurred at state level are borne solely using state resources. Putrajaya also channels funds via a state road maintenance grant, known as Marris, to help finance maintenance work on state roads.
Under Budget 2026, the federal government allocated RM2.5 billion for federal road maintenance, but also provided RM5.6 billion through Marris for the maintenance of state roads nationwide.
Universiti Kuala Lumpur economist Aimi Zulhazmi Abdul Rashid said responsibility for water supply was not confined to a single authority.
Water resources and rivers remain under state jurisdiction, while water services and supply in the peninsula and Labuan fall under the concurrent list following a constitutional amendment in 2005.

Aimi said this could create what is known as a “split incentive”, where the party that provides capital for infrastructure development does not necessarily receive the direct benefit or return from the investment.

He said the public should also look at the scale of a problem to understand which party was more closely linked to it. Issues affecting a wider supply chain may require federal involvement, he said, while localised issues are more closely tied to state administration.
Hospitals, schools
Health and education are among the core areas under federal jurisdiction, even though hospitals, clinics and schools are physically located and operate within the states.

Under Budget 2026, the federal government allocated RM46.5 billion to the health ministry, including RM1.2 billion for the maintenance and repair of government hospitals and clinics, and RM100 million to upgrade wards at district hospitals.
For education and training, federal expenditure in 2026 is estimated at RM74.37 billion.
Sabah and Sarawak
The division of powers is slightly different for Sabah and Sarawak, as both states enjoy additional powers under the constitution.
In addition to the standard state and concurrent lists, the two East Malaysian states also have a supplementary state and concurrent list, which grant them greater autonomy in certain areas.
Ramli said this stems from the agreement reached for the formation of Malaysia in 1963.
However, he said it did not mean that the federal government was no longer involved in financing development and services in the two states.
Under Budget 2026, Sabah and Sarawak received the highest federal development allocations, at RM6.9 billion and RM6 billion respectively.

In November 2024, then minister in the Prime Minister’s Department for federal territories, Dr Zaliha Mustafa, said Sabah led the country with 1,244 federal development projects while Sarawak had 1,124.
However, their spending rates as of October that year stood at only 46.7% and 54.43%, respectively, due to slow project implementation.

Factors such as land acquisition, logistical hurdles, difficult terrain and poor coordination between agencies often explain why spending lags behind allocations, rather than reflecting inadequate federal funding.
c8f05ed17814a918: PETALING JAYA: Masyarakat tidak seharusnya menganggap semua masalah infrastruktur menjadi tanggungjawab satu pihak sahaja kerana bidang kuasa, pelaksanaan dan pembiayaannya boleh melibatkan kerajaan persekutuan dan negeri.

Ahli akademik Ramli Dollah daripada Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) berkata, pembahagian tanggungjawab antara kedua-dua peringkat kerajaan secara asasnya sudah ditetapkan dalam Perlembagaan Persekutuan.

Pensyarah di Fakulti Sains Sosial dan Kemanusiaan itu menekankan pembahagian kuasa itu ditetapkan menerusi Senarai Persekutuan, Senarai Negeri dan Senarai Bersama dalam Jadual Kesembilan Perlembagaan Persekutuan.
“Rakyat perlu berhati-hati supaya tidak terus menganggap semua masalah infrastruktur adalah tanggungjawab satu kerajaan sahaja.

“Kita perlu bezakan tiga perkara: siapa mempunyai bidang kuasa, siapa melaksanakan projek dan siapa menyediakan wang. Kadang-kadang tiga perkara ini melibatkan kerajaan yang berbeza,” katanya kepada FMT.
Secara umum bidang seperti pertahanan, keselamatan dalam negeri, pendidikan serta perubatan dan kesihatan berada di bawah kerajaan persekutuan.

Sementara itu, negeri pula bertanggungjawab dalam aspek tanah, pertanian, perhutanan dan kerajaan tempatan manakala kedua-duanya mengurus kebajikan masyarakat, perancangan bandar dan desa serta beberapa aspek kesihatan awam.
Sehubungan itu, Ramli menekankan pembahagian itu bermakna sesuatu masalah tidak boleh dikaitkan dengan kerajaan tertentu hanya berdasarkan lokasi ia berlaku.
Sebagai contoh, tanah dan perhutanan merupakan bidang kuasa negeri yang bermaksud isu berkaitan pengurusan hutan sert sumber balak perlu dilihat berdasarkan tanggungjawab kerajaan negeri berkenaan.
Pada masa sama, kerajaan persekutuan turut menyalurkan pelbagai bentuk pemberian kepada negeri untuk membantu membiayai tanggungjawab dan pembangunan di peringkat negeri.
Mac lalu, Majlis Kewangan Negara (MKewN) bersetuju menambah baik pemberian kerajaan persekutuan kepada negeri yang dijangka mencecah RM10.5 bilion tahun ini, berbanding RM10.3 bilion pada 2025.
Antaranya melibatkan Pemberian Senarai Bersama, Pemberian Penyenggaraan Jalan Negeri dan agihan Cukai Pelancongan.
Jalan dan bekalan air
Jalan raya antara contoh paling mudah untuk melihat bagaimana tanggungjawab antara kerajaan persekutuan dan negeri dibahagikan.
Jalan persekutuan berada di bawah tanggungjawab kerajaan persekutuan, manakala jalan negeri diuruskan kerajaan negeri dan jalan tertentu pula berada di bawah pihak berkuasa tempatan (PBT).
Namun, tanggungjawab negeri terhadap jalan tidak bermakna semua kos ditanggung menggunakan sumber negeri.
Putrajaya turut menyalurkan Pemberian Penyenggaraan Jalan Negeri (MARRIS) untuk membantu membiayai kerja penyenggaraan jalan negeri.
Dalam Belanjawan 2026, kerajaan persekutuan menyediakan RM5.6 bilion menerusi MARRIS bagi penyenggaraan jalan negeri di seluruh negara, selain RM2.5 bilion untuk penyenggaraan jalan persekutuan.
Bagi bekalan air pula, ahli ekonomi Aimi Zulhazmi Abdul Rashid daripada Universiti Kuala Lumpur pula berkata tanggungjawabnya turut melibatkan lebih daripada satu pihak.
Sumber air dan sungai kekal di bawah bidang kuasa negeri, manakala perkhidmatan serta bekalan air di Semenanjung dan Labuan berada dalam Senarai Bersama selepas pindaan Perlembagaan pada 2005.

Menurut Aimi, keadaan itu boleh mewujudkan apa yang dikenali sebagai “split incentive”, apabila pihak yang menyediakan modal bagi pembangunan infrastruktur tidak semestinya menerima manfaat atau pulangan secara langsung daripada pelaburan itu.

Katanya, rakyat juga boleh melihat skala sesuatu masalah untuk memahami pihak yang lebih berkait dengannya, dengan isu melibatkan rantaian bekalan lebih luas boleh memerlukan penglibatan persekutuan, manakala isu setempat lebih dekat dengan pentadbiran negeri.
Sekolah dan hospital
Pendidikan dan kesihatan pula antara bidang utama di bawah kerajaan persekutuan walaupun sekolah, hospital dan klinik kerajaan terletak serta beroperasi di negeri.
Ini bermakna kewujudan sesebuah sekolah atau hospital dalam negeri tertentu tidak secara automatik menjadikannya tanggungjawab kerajaan negeri.

Dalam Belanjawan 2026, kerajaan persekutuan memperuntukkan RM46.5 bilion kepada Kementerian Kesihatan, termasuk RM1.2 bilion bagi penyenggaraan dan baik pulih hospital serta klinik kerajaan dan RM100 juta untuk menaik taraf wad hospital daerah.
Bagi sektor pelajaran dan latihan pula, perbelanjaan persekutuan pada 2026 dianggarkan RM74.37 bilion.
Sabah dan Sarawak
Namun, pembahagian kuasa sedikit berbeza bagi Sabah dan Sarawak kerana kedua-duanya mempunyai bidang kuasa tambahan yang diperuntukkan dalam Perlembagaan Persekutuan.
Selain Senarai Negeri dan Senarai Bersama, kedua-dua negeri mempunyai Senarai Tambahan kepada Senarai Negeri dan Senarai Tambahan kepada Senarai Bersama.

Ramli berkata kedudukan itu berkait dengan pembentukan Malaysia pada 1963, yang menyaksikan Sabah dan Sarawak mempunyai beberapa bidang kuasa serta sumber hasil berbeza berbanding negeri di Semenanjung.
Namun, katanya, bidang kuasa dan sumber hasil tambahan itu tidak bermakna kerajaan persekutuan tidak lagi terlibat dalam membiayai pembangunan serta perkhidmatan di kedua-dua negeri.
Dalam Belanjawan 2026, Sabah dan Sarawak menerima peruntukan pembangunan persekutuan tertinggi, masing-masing RM6.9 bilion dan RM6 bilion.

Pada November 2024, Menteri di Jabatan Perdana Menteri (Wilayah Persekutuan) ketika itu, Dr Zaliha Mustafa, berkata Sabah merekodkan 1,244 projek pembangunan persekutuan manakala Sarawak mempunyai 1,124 projek, tertinggi di negara ini.
Namun, kadar perbelanjaan setakat Oktober tahun berkenaan masing-masing hanya 46.7% dan 54.43%.
Antara faktor yang boleh melambatkan pelaksanaan projek termasuk pengambilan tanah, masalah logistik, bentuk muka bumi yang mencabar serta penyelarasan antara agensi.
Justeru, kadar perbelanjaan yang rendah tidak semestinya berpunca daripada kekurangan peruntukan persekutuan, sebaliknya boleh dipengaruhi pelbagai kekangan pada peringkat pelaksanaan.
8effd2eb7d7008d9: KUALA LUMPUR: It is a sweltering afternoon at the ARBA Equestrian Archery Academy in Ulu Yam, where a group of teenagers are taking turns to ride their horses along a trail.
As they thunder down the track, the young archers raise their bows, take aim and release arrows. It looks like a scene right out of a fantasy film.
Among the riders is Abdurrahman Ahmad Muaz, 16, who effortlessly hits a target further down the course. Watching on, his mother and coach, Nurul Fathim Ridayu Ramli, smiles proudly.
Abdurrahman is an accomplished horseback archer who has made a name for himself on the international stage.
Most recently, he made headlines after clinching a gold medal in the Open Tower 90 category at the International Horseback Archery Masters 2026, held from Oct 1-4 in Erenhot, Inner Mongolia, China.

“I feel my performance in China wasn’t as good as it usually is back home. It was challenging there because of the freezing temperatures and strong winds. Still, I’m proud of myself that I managed to win,” he told FMT Lifestyle.
Abdurrahman has been involved in horseback archery for about four years. Interestingly, he never originally intended to pursue the sport: in fact, it was his mother who introduced him to it.
According to Nurul Fathim, 41, horseback riding had always been in her bucket list. For her birthday in 2022, she finally gave it a go, bringing her children along for the experience.

Little did she know that her children would love it more than she did. Later, they took a shot at archery and loved that too. It was only natural then that they would combine both these passions into horseback archery.
Today, most of the family remains passionate about the sport, with five of her six children, including Abdurrahman, regularly attending horseback riding or horseback archery lessons.

Nurul Fathim said she was happy about this as horseback riding and archery is widely regarded as sunnah sports, activities associated with Islamic teachings that promote physical fitness, discipline and perseverance.

Abdurrahman regularly trains at the ARBA Equestrian Archery Academy founded by his mother. His daily training regimen includes at least an hour of archery practice and another hour of horseback riding.

His passion has taken him far: Abdurrahman has won numerous accolades in the sport, including a gold medal in the Under-16 category of the International Horseback Archery Alliance (IHAA) World Kids Championship in Indonesia, and a silver at the Asian Junior Horseback Archery Championship in Kazakhstan.
Abdurrahman, however, considers his victory in China his greatest achievement, particularly given the challenges he had to overcome on the road to victory.

As their invitation to the competition had arrived at short notice, he and his mother had to fund the trip to China themselves. And while many of the other competitors were accompanied by full support teams, Abdurrahman only had his mother by his side, leaving him somewhat sad and disheartened.
Nevertheless, he put these feelings aside and focussed on the competition, determined to do Malaysia proud.

His resolve paid off. Despite being considerably younger than many of his opponents, Abdurrahman outperformed some of the world's finest, including seasoned competitors from France and Mongolia, to emerge victorious.

His secret to success? No time for horsing around: horseback archery requires constant and diligent training, and a good bond with your animal. While he trains with several horses, Abdurrahman has a soft spot for his horse Luhaif.

“You should spend time with your horse, and go play or walk with them. Before an event, some people like to leave preparing their horse to others. I like to groom my horse, put on his saddle, make him feel comfortable with me,” Abdurrahman said.

Horseback archery may still be a niche sport in Malaysia, but Abdurrahman hopes it will gain popularity in the future. He dreams of someday owning a riding club “with 20 horses”, and keep winning medals for the country.
“Horseback archery is a great sport, and very good exercise. I hope one day it is included in the Olympics,” concluded Abdurrahman with a smile.
ad531227c8cd2ee6: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Nearly RM11 billion in Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) assistance had been disbursed to eligible recipients as of September 2026, according to the Ministry of Finance (MoF).
MoF said that RM3.6 billion had been disbursed to STR recipients through three payment phases as of last month.

The ministry said the government continues to ensure that the RM15 billion allocated for STR and Sara in 2026 delivers tangible benefits to the people, especially low-income groups and vulnerable communities.
“This year, nearly nine million citizens are eligible to receive Sara monthly, while STR is distributed quarterly to eligible households and the elderly.

“The effectiveness of the implementation of STR and Sara can be accessed through several aspects, including recipient coverage, aid utilisation, targeting accuracy and the ability of the aid to meet basic needs,” it said in a written response published on the Parliament website.

MoF said this in response to Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin’s (PN-Pagoh) question regarding the effectiveness of the RM15 billion allocation for STR and Sara based on basic spending and its distribution to low-income citizens.
The ministry noted that the monthly Sara recorded a utilisation rate of 99.7 per cent, with a transaction value of RM5.2 billion as of September 2026.

Meanwhile, for Sara Untuk Semua, more than 20 million citizens had made purchases, representing 90 per cent of the total number of recipients, with transaction values in the local market amounting to nearly RM1.9 billion, it added. — Bernama
8c76608ab9690fb8: JAKARTA, Oct 20 — Indonesian police have confirmed the involvement of foreign entities, including those from neighbouring countries, in 98 corporate cases linked to the forest and land fires gripping the country.
National Police Chief General Suyudi Ario Seto said the Criminal Investigation Agency (Bareskrim) is currently working to identify those responsible and establish the nature of their involvement.

“Of the 98 corporate cases we are investigating, there is foreign involvement, but as the investigations are ongoing, we are still determining which involve foreign investment or foreign parties and which do not,” he told a press conference after a limited Cabinet meeting with President Prabowo Subianto in Jakarta on Monday.
Suyudi said investigators are gathering evidence and expected to name suspects soon, including company owners and shareholders who could be held responsible for the fires.

Separately, Coordinating Minister for Political and Security Affairs Dudung Abdurachman Prabowo called for firefighting operations to be intensified without waiting for rainfall, stressing the need for immediate and sustained action.

“The president instructed that the deployment of troops and personnel, including the Indonesian military, police, Forestry Service, and members of the public, be intensified. This must be carried out on a massive scale, in a measured manner and without delay, because the situation has become very disruptive,” he said.

Dudung also said Indonesia had responded to offers of foreign assistance, including from Malaysia and Singapore, with the National Disaster Management Agency (BNPB) coordinating technical arrangements for the proposed support.

However, he said at an earlier press conference that foreign assistance would have to wait until the Indonesian government declares the fires a national disaster — a step it has yet to take, saying it was capable of managing the crisis with its own resources. — Bernama

fbbd584b4132dccb: PASIR PUTEH: Police and animal welfare activists have removed several cats from the home of a suspect arrested after a video showing him committing an indecent act involving a cat went viral.
District police chief Superintendent Saari Yaacob said the animals were relocated to ensure their safety following the 49-year-old suspect's arrest at 10am yesterday.
The cat involved in the incident was handed over to the Veterinary Services Department for further examination.
Saari said police are investigating the suspect's mental health status following claims that he has psychological issues.
"We have yet to receive medical confirmation or documentation regarding his condition.
"To protect the remaining cats from harm, we have moved them to a care centre," he said when met in Selinsing last night.
The suspect was detained after a 56-second video showing the alleged act triggered public outrage online.

Saari warned the public against sharing the video, noting that offenders face action under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998, which carries a maximum fine of RM500,000, up to two years' imprisonment, or both.
Meanwhile, animal welfare activist Nur Izyan Syahida Rosli said she had taken two cats from the suspect's home to be cared for under the Kelab Pencinta Haiwan Pewaris Kelantan.
She added that the group is prepared to adopt the cat involved in the incident once police complete their investigation.
"We are ready to take in the cat if permitted by the authorities after investigations conclude," she said.
ae7352c73dcc5a8e: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The Finance Ministry (MoF) has not made any commitment to provide financial assistance to AirAsia Bhd, whether in the form of guarantees, financing or injection of public funds.

The ministry said applications for government support from any companies will be considered based on the interests of the country and the people, fiscal sustainability and the protection of public funds, in accordance with prevailing laws and procedures.

It also said the government will not comment on any speculation or figures reported by the media to avoid affecting the market and the interests of employees, customers and other stakeholders of the companies concerned.
“The government will continue to monitor the developments closely, while prioritising the people’s interest,” it said in a written reply to the Dewan Rakyat, published on the Parliament’s website.
The MoF was responding to a question from Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong (BN-Ayer Hitam) on whether the government is considering providing any guarantees, loans or public funds to AirAsia.
The ministry said the government has taken note of issues raised concerning AirAsia, including the losses reported in its latest quarterly financial results.
The airline had mainly attributed its losses to the spike in jet fuel prices due to the West Asia conflict.

“The government regularly engages with players across the aviation industry as part of its monitoring efforts, to seek input from industry players, technical experts and other parties, as it has also done for other economic sectors affected by the West Asia crisis,” it said.
On September 19, Bernama reported that AirAsia had not held any discussions with the government on a “bailout” and remained confident in its liquidity position and business sustainability. — Bernama
9b8abc5dc11df495: HOUSTON: Early voting began Monday in Texas, home to some of the most closely watched races in November's midterm elections, with Democrats hopeful for historic victories in the traditional Republican stronghold.
Lines formed early at a Houston polling station, as Texas voters weighed a choice between Democrats campaigning on economic concerns and Republicans aligned with US President Donald Trump.
In the governor's race, polls indicate a slight lead for Democrat Gina Hinojosa, a 52-year-old attorney who seeks to beat incumbent Greg Abbott, a 68-year-old Republican running for a fourth term.
"We have never been so close," Hinojosa said Sunday. "If we don't win this time, they will never let us get this close again."
In the US Senate race, Democrat James Talarico, a 37-year-old former teacher, has energized voters to gain a slight lead over Trump ally and Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, 63.

Hinojosa and Talarico represent a new generation of Democrats who are seeking to attract independents and voters disillusioned by Trump's unpopular war in the Middle East and skyrocketing prices for gas and everyday goods.
Democrats are also counting on winning back Latino support from Trump, who made gains in the 2024 election but is now facing growing discontent over immigration raids, polling shows.
Republicans are counting on voters who support Trump to turn out the vote, as the president has asked them to.

"I want Donald Trump to finish," Rose Mary Cuevas, 64, said. "I want him to finish up what he said he's gonna do and I just hope that everything works out for the best and thank Jesus Christ for that."
Both Abbott and Paxton have avoided debates ahead of the polls.

Paxton is seeking to overcome years of controversy, including long-running securities fraud charges that were resolved without an admission of wrongdoing, allegations of infidelity surrounding the collapse of his marriage, and questions about his ties to wealthy donors.
In 2023, the Republican-controlled Texas House impeached Paxton over corruption and abuse of power allegations. He was later acquitted by the state Senate.
Paxton also backed Trump in 2020, when the president contested his loss to Joe Biden without offering evidence.
As early voters headed to polls, a federal prosecutor in Texas, Aaron Reitz, issued a warning.
"Only eligible voters can vote. No barred felons, no aliens and no foreigners," Reitz said in a video on X. "If you violate federal election law, I will hunt you down and prosecute you."
eb1651581dd3cef8: PETALING JAYA: PAS has played down the need to name a poster boy for the Melaka state election, with deputy president Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man saying the chief minister should come from the party that wins the most seats.
Tuan Ibrahim said PAS was focused on securing the people’s mandate, Utusan Malaysia reported.
He said the issue of a poster boy was sometimes "deliberately turned into a polemic", and that leaders should be chosen based on ability and suitability rather than popularity.
"For example, who knew (Terengganu menteri besar) Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar before this? Likewise in Kedah, who knew (Kedah menteri besar) Sanusi Nor?
"Their names were not well known before. This shows that choosing a leader must be based on the individual’s ability and suitability, not merely popularity," he was quoted as saying.
When asked if PAS would accept a poster boy candidate from another party, Tuan Ibrahim said the matter would be discussed with the parties it works with.
"Whether there will be a poster boy for the Melaka polls will be discussed and decided by the party based on a joint decision.
"For now, our priority is the manifesto, not the question of the poster boy," he said.
The Election Commission has fixed Nov 14 as polling day, with nomination on Oct 31 and early voting on Nov 10.
All 28 seats in the state assembly are up for grabs. In the 2021 election, Barisan Nasional won 21 seats while Pakatan Harapan took five and Perikatan Nasional two.
24fe7bc2261e92a3: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The government is refining proposals to improve the National Haze Action Plan, particularly regarding school closure directives and the Ministry of Education’s (MOE) early preparations to ensure learning can continue if schools are forced to close.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, via a Facebook post yesterday, said the health of children remains the government’s top priority while ensuring their education is not disrupted.

He said the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), the Department of Environment, and the Malaysian Meteorological Department will refine these proposals together with the MOE and the Ministry of Health (MOH).

“I also emphasised that allocation requirements for cloud seeding operations will be fulfilled to reduce the haze. These operations are currently being carried out almost daily, depending on suitable cloud conditions,” he said in the post.

Earlier, the Prime Minister chaired a National Disaster Management Council meeting, which discussed in detail the current and concerning haze situation as well as its impact on public health, especially school going children.

Anwar said the meeting was also briefed on the country’s preparations to face the North-east Monsoon, which is expected to bring heavy rain and flood risks, as well as the threat of a Super El Nino forecasted to bring extreme hot and dry weather next year.

“Accordingly, the preparedness of frontline agencies must continue to be enhanced. Nadma must be empowered as the pulse of cross-agency policy and operational coordination, particularly through the Central Disaster Operations Control Centre, so that prevention, preparation, response, and recovery measures can be implemented swiftly and effectively,” he said.
He added that the Federal and State Governments, the private sector, volunteers, and the community must move together to strengthen community preparedness.
“The lives of the people must be protected, and aid must reach those in need immediately. This is the trust that we must shoulder together,” he said. — Bernama
5913c2be2f005fe1: BENGALURU: Oil prices fell on Tuesday as markets weighed an executive order by US President Donald Trump waiving some sanctions and tariffs linked to Russian energy exports, while attacks on Saudi Arabia and Yemen kept concerns over Middle East supply disruptions in focus.
Brent crude futures fell 49 cents, or 0.45 per cent, to US$109.06 a barrel by 8.10am Malaysian time.

The US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude contract for November delivery, which expires on Tuesday, eased 0.33 per cent to US$103.32. The more actively traded December contract fell 46 cents, or 0.47 per cent, to US$98.08.
Brent rose to US$110.70 a barrel in the previous session, its highest since May 20.

An executive order issued by Trump on Friday night waived key US sanctions and tariffs related to Russia, including duties on the country's goods and penalties for buying its oil and gas. However, Trump said on Saturday that he had yet to make a final decision on the matter, while Secretary of State Marco Rubio said officials wanted more time to evaluate the situation.

Russia's crude oil production rose by 65,000 barrels per day in September to 8.43 million barrels per day, but remained about 870,000 barrels per day below a year earlier, the International Energy Agency said last week.

"While the prospect of additional Russian diesel supply offers some theoretical relief, traders appear far more focused on the ongoing risk of further damage to energy infrastructure across the Gulf region," KCM Trade chief analyst Tim Waterer said.

Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said on Monday they had carried out several attacks on Saudi energy, airport and military targets, including an Aramco site in Yanbu, the Shaybah oilfield, King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and Abha airport.
Saudi authorities did not immediately confirm the claims, and Reuters could not independently verify them.
Meanwhile, 58 people were killed and more than 200 injured in a Houthi attack on a government security forces training camp in Yemen's Shabwa province on Monday.
The renewed attacks heightened concerns over regional stability and underscored the continuing risks to energy supplies from the region, keeping oil prices above US$100 a barrel.
In the US, crude oil stockpiles were expected to have fallen last week, along with inventories of refined products, a preliminary Reuters poll showed on Monday.
71d4c9e443291ec4: EDMONTON: Vote counting was underway in Canada's province of Alberta on Monday, as the oil-rich province decided whether to hold a binding independence referendum, testing national unity amid a crisis in relations with the United States.

Prime Minister Mark Carney has in recent days argued that Alberta's vote is being held "at the worst possible time", urging Canadians to rally together to confront US President Donald Trump's trade war and annexation threats.
Polls indicated that less than a quarter of people in the western province wanted independence, but separatist leader Mitch Sylvestre told AFP on Monday that he remained optimistic.
"We're hoping to win," said Sylvestre, who heads the Alberta Prosperity Project, at a restaurant in the provincial capital, Edmonton, where his side was watching the returns.
Most polling stations were due to close at 8pm (0200 GMT Tuesday), but more than 100 would close later because of delayed openings, Alberta's elections authority said.
Elections Alberta said 1.4 million of the 3.1 million eligible voters had cast advance ballots. Those ballots were being counted from 5pm.
Results might not be available until the early hours of Tuesday, Elections Alberta said.
David Gallagher, who voted earlier on a chilly Edmonton morning, told AFP that an independent Alberta was a "silly idea".
"I want to stamp it down and stop it," the 58-year-old said.
Alberta Premier Danielle Smith, a conservative, has said she will vote against independence but called the referendum to settle an issue that has divided the province.
If a majority votes to separate, she has pledged to move forward with a binding referendum.
If the federalists win, Smith said the secession question should be considered closed.
Foreign influence?
Alberta has the world's fourth-largest proven oil reserves, and much of the separatist momentum has been driven by anger over the management of the oil industry.
Smith has blamed Carney's predecessor, Justin Trudeau, for igniting the separatist movement, accusing him of trying to crush oil production to advance his pro-climate agenda.
Alberta's independence push has also drawn sustained interest from Trump allies.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called Alberta a "natural partner" for the United States. Elon Musk, the world's richest person and a top Trump supporter, posted on X this month that Alberta "should separate".
Separatist leaders have also held meetings at the US State Department and with Republican political operatives.
'Huge uncertainty'
Carney, who grew up in Alberta, has worked to improve relations between the province and Ottawa since taking office last year.
He has partnered with Smith to advance a new pipeline to export more Alberta bitumen overseas, a project considered a non-starter during Trudeau's tenure.
But he has also warned Albertans that even a non-binding vote on independence would be a "dangerous bluff", drawing on his experience during Brexit, when he was governor of the Bank of England.
He said the "huge uncertainty" that followed the Brexit vote hurt the British economy, cautioning Alberta against unintended economic consequences.
Sylvestre said Carney had "threatened" the province in the closing days of the campaign.
Carney's message was "voting against Canada is dangerous", Sylvestre said. "I think that's very, very unreasonable."
Haley Erdegard, a 44-year-old who voted in Edmonton, voiced discomfort with the idea advanced by some separatists that Alberta was forced to share too much of its oil revenue with the rest of Canada.
"The whole point of privilege is that if you have more than somebody else, you're supposed to share," she told AFP.
"I think we probably need to put some more work towards cooperation before making rash decisions about trying to start our own country."

a3c301db964d613d: SINGAPORE, Oct 20 — Firefly will fully resume its flights between Subang and Singapore on Thursday (October 22), following its latest operational assessment of weather and haze conditions in Singapore.

In an advisory on Monday, the airline said it would operate a reduced flight schedule between Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport in Subang and Seletar Airport on October 21 before restoring full services the following day.

“Affected passengers are being contacted and offered alternative travel arrangements on available Malaysia Airlines flights between Kuala Lumpur (KUL) and Singapore (SIN), subject to seat availability.
“Passengers who choose not to proceed with the alternative arrangements are eligible for a full refund,” it said.
The wholly owned subsidiary of Malaysia Airlines had earlier cancelled all scheduled flights between the two airports up until Monday.
The flights scheduled to resume on October 21 are FY3122 and FY3123, FY3126 and FY3127, and FY3130 and FY3131.
Singapore’s air quality improved on Monday, with the 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) ranging from 86 to 115 as of 11pm, according to the National Environment Agency (NEA). — Bernama
579154ebc85ef75d: MACHANG: A 26-year-old woman was killed when her car was rammed by a trailer that ran a red light at Km4.7 of Jalan Machang-Tanah Merah, near the Wakaf Bata traffic light junction, here last night.
In the 10.30pm incident, the victim died at the scene from severe injuries.
District police chief Superintendent Azuhar Md Nor said initial investigations revealed that the Volvo trailer, driven by a 47-year-old man, was travelling from Tanah Merah towards Machang.
"The trailer is believed to have run a red light at the junction before crashing into the right side of the Perodua Axia, which was moving from Padang Kelupang towards Tanah Merah.
"The heavy impact caused the Perodua Axia driver to suffer severe injuries, and she was pronounced dead at the scene.
"The trailer driver was unhurt," he said in a statement today.
He added that the victim's body was sent to Sultan Ismail Petra Hospital in Kuala Krai for an autopsy.
"The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for causing death by reckless and dangerous driving.

"The trailer driver was also arrested under Section 30 of the Poisons Act 1952 after police seized four transparent plastic packages containing a brownish liquid suspected to be ketum water," he said.
Those with information can contact Machang district police headquarters traffic investigating officer Inspector Khairulanwar Adam at 011-10085165 or visit the nearest police station.
f27fe1c30afd42dc: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump's administration has reached a settlement deal with the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill to close 18 federal probes over alleged race discrimination and antisemitism at the university.

Trump has targeted universities with probes and funding-suspension ​threats over pro-Palestinian protests against US ally Israel's assault on ​Gaza, diversity initiatives, transgender policies and climate programmes, leading to free speech, due process and academic freedom concerns.

The voluntary settlement agreement released by both parties does not require a monetary settlement payment and will remain effective until the end of 2028. UNC did not admit to any wrongdoing or liability, and the deal maintained its eligibility for federal funding.

The agreement said UNC will appoint an internal administrator and establish a coordinator position in its compliance office to address discrimination, including antisemitism. The agreement asks UNC to provide mandatory antisemitism training to students, faculty and staff.

The university said Elizabeth Hall, associate vice chancellor for university compliance, was appointed to serve in both roles while being the point of contact for the Justice Department and overseeing UNC's reporting obligations under the deal.
The agreement prohibited face masks or coverings concealing an individual's identity during protests. It said student groups "shall be subject to discipline for antisemitic discriminatory conduct."
Trump has alleged pro-Palestinian protesters are antisemitic and support extremism.

Protesters, including some Jewish groups, say opposing Israel's occupation of Palestinian territories and its assault on Gaza is not antisemitic and advocacy for Palestinian rights does not imply supporting extremism.

A former justice department attorney said in a whistleblower complaint in August the Trump administration's probes of universities over antisemitism accusations lacked evidence and had predetermined outcomes.
The settlement deal said UNC will adopt and maintain "non-discriminatory" admissions policies and "not use any racial proxy".

It does not prevent UNC from considering how applicants overcame adversity at a personal level, and it may consider facets of family background like poverty if those considerations are applied consistently, the deal said.
The justice department said that on a quarterly basis, UNC will send any antisemitism and race discrimination complaints it has received to the US justice and education departments.
The Supreme Court rejected affirmative action at colleges in 2023 when it struck down ​race-conscious admissions programmes at Harvard and UNC.

Trump has cracked down on diversity initiatives, casting them as discriminatory against white people and men. Civil rights advocates say they help marginalised groups like ethnic minorities, LGBT communities and women.
The government has also settled with some other schools.

Last year, Columbia University agreed to pay more than US$200 million to the government to resolve probes, and Brown University said it would pay US$50 million to support local workforce development under a settlement.
Harvard has yet to make a deal.
06a37e8fa213becd: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Tuesday despite a stronger greenback, supported by easing domestic inflation and expectations of a possible normalisation of the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR).
At 8am, the ringgit strengthened to 4.0780/0850 against the US dollar, compared with Monday's close of 4.0805/0845.
The Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) reported that inflation eased to 1.8 per cent in September 2026, from 1.9 per cent in August.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid expected the ringgit to trade within a range of RM4.07 to RM4.08 against the US dollar today.
He said investors were also monitoring geopolitical risks in West Asia after Iran's navy reported an attack by the US military on the Konarak naval base.
"We are entering the blackout period, during which US Federal Reserve officials will not be commenting publicly ahead of next week's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting," he told Bernama.
The US Dollar Index (DXY), which measures the greenback against a basket of major currencies, rose 0.15 per cent to 101.989 points, he added.

At the opening, the ringgit traded mostly higher against major currencies. It strengthened against the Japanese yen to 2.5724/5770 from 2.5790/5817 at Monday's close, and rose against the British pound to 5.4274/4367 from 5.4369/4422.
However, it edged lower against the euro to 4.5731/5809 from 4.5726/5771 previously.
The ringgit also strengthened against most of its ASEAN peers.
It edged up against the Indonesian rupiah to 225.9/226.4 from 226.0/226.4 on Monday, and against the Philippine peso to 6.46/6.48 from 6.47/6.48.
The local currency also rose against the Singapore dollar to 3.1862/1919 from 3.1886/1920 at the previous close, and strengthened against the Thai baht to 12.1373/1661 from 12.1451/1613.
fd59e71618fe9642: ARAU: The haze affecting Malaysia is expected to gradually improve by the end of this month as the country enters the monsoon transition phase, which could bring more rain and changes in wind direction and speed.

Universiti Malaysia Perlis (Unimap) Faculty of Civil Engineering and Technology associate professor Dr Norazian Mohamed Noor said these factors could help reduce atmospheric pollutant concentrations and limit the cross-border movement of smoke from Indonesia.

She said the Malaysian Meteorological Department's (MetMalaysia) long-range weather outlook for October to March 2027 indicated that most parts of the country were expected to receive rainfall close to their climatological averages from this month until December.
Selangor, for example, was forecast to receive between 220mm and 330mm of rain this month, and between 250mm and 380mm in November.
Kuala Lumpur, meanwhile, was expected to receive between 240mm and 360mm of rain in October, rising to between 300mm and 450mm in November.
"These conditions offer a positive indication that increased rainfall could help improve air quality in Malaysia. However, the recovery may not occur simultaneously across all areas.
"Haze conditions are influenced not only by rainfall in Malaysia but also by fire activity, rainfall distribution in pollution-source areas and wind direction.
"Rainfall in our country alone is insufficient to ensure an end to transboundary haze if fires remain active at their source in Indonesia," she said recently.

Norazian said an analysis by Indonesia's Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency (BMKG), dated Oct 13, indicated that parts of southern Sumatra, West Kalimantan, Central Kalimantan and South Kalimantan were still expected to receive low rainfall of less than 50mm over certain 10-day periods this month.
She said the conditions could increase the risk of forest and peatland fires, particularly in areas experiencing prolonged dry spells.

"However, the BMKG forecast also indicated increased rainfall in several parts of Sumatra and Kalimantan in November and December, with some areas potentially receiving more than 300mm of rain a month.
"Should the rainfall be continuous and cover fire-affected areas, it could help reduce fire activity and smoke emissions," she said.
e7f805a587db6ca0: KUALA TERENGGANU: A 46-year-old housewife here lost RM472,000 after falling victim to a phone scam syndicate.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Azli Mohd Noor said the victim lodged a police report at 10.30am yesterday.
On Aug 5, the woman received a call from an individual identifying himself as "Mohd Farhan Jamil", claiming to be from the Communications Ministry.
The caller informed her that she was involved in spreading unauthorised information regarding investment shares, government assistance, and job opportunities.
"The individual then claimed her call was being transferred to the Kajang police headquarters, where she spoke to 'Sergeant Andi'.

"The suspect impersonating Sergeant Andi instructed the victim to read out her identity card number. After performing a 'check', he claimed she was involved in money laundering activities," Azli said.
The suspect also told her that an arrest warrant had been issued in her name.

The call was subsequently transferred to a deputy public prosecutor named Zaleha. To resolve the matter, Zaleha instructed the victim to transfer funds, promising the money would be returned upon completion of the investigation.
Fearing arrest, the victim made 21 transactions into three separate bank accounts between Aug 18 and Sept 19, amounting to RM472,000.
"After completing the payments, she was asked to transfer an additional RM80,000, but she refused. Realising she had been cheated, she lodged a police report," Azli added.
The funds involved were the victim's personal savings.
The case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating.

9bbef9d48d222070: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Allegations of “corporate mafia” activities and abuse of power involving the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) are among the issues to be raised in the Dewan Rakyat today.

According to the Order Paper on Parliament’s official portal, during Minister’s Question Time, Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun (PH-Port Dickson) will ask the Prime Minister for an update on “corporate mafia” allegations involving violations of the law and the action taken so far.

Ahmad Fadhli Shaari (PN-Pasir Mas) will ask the Prime Minister for an update on investigations into alleged misappropriation, corruption and abuse of power involving Felda, including its subsidiary Felda Investment Corporation.

Tan Kar Hing (PH-Gopeng) will also ask the Agriculture and Food Security Minister about the outcomes of the Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism Exhibition 2026, as well as the added value and follow-up investments expected to materialise from the memoranda of understanding signed.

Datuk Idris Ahmad (PN-Bagan Serai) will ask the Prime Minister whether the government is prepared to make merit-based appointments free from political influence, a key governance policy for Tabung Haji, in line with one of the Royal Commission of Inquiry's recommendations.

The calendar for the Third Meeting of the Fifth Session of the 15th Parliament shows that the policy-stage debate on Budget 2027 is scheduled for October 12 to 22, with the relevant ministers to wind up the debate over four days from October 26.

2c3781b7fa908d2b: GQEBERHA, South Africa: Scott Boland does not get many chances to bowl for Australia in Test matches, but he showed again on Monday that when he gets the call he is ready to step up.
Boland took four for 31 to have South Africa tottering at 97 for five after two rain-hit days of the second Test at St George's Park.

"I like to play every game I can," the 37-year-old said, but admitted it was not always possible with Australia having three world-class fast bowlers ahead of him in skipper Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood.
All four seamers are in the top ten of the world Test bowling rankings.
But Boland got his opportunity in Gqeberha when Australia opted for an all-seam attack.

Although he had not played in a first-class match since March and had not appeared in a Test match since January, Boland said he kept sharp by working hard before the tour and during net practices since the team arrived in South Africa.
"My mindset is to find my line and length quickly," he said.
Boland did that to devastating effect when he took both wickets as South Africa slipped to 20 for two on a rain-ruined first day.
Then he struck early on Monday – after rain delayed the start of play by six hours – and again shortly before the close.

Boland's relentless accuracy left world Test champions South Africa in a precarious position as they sought to play their way back into the three-match series after losing the first Test in Durban by 214 runs.
"He doesn't miss his spot very often," said South African batting coach Ashwell Prince in comparing Boland to former South African opening bowler Vernon Philander.
"His balls are always on or around the top of the stumps so there's always that uncertainty (for batters)."
But Prince said he expected the South African bowlers to be similarly threatening.
"The ball is moving around and the pitch is a bit soft so there are some divots around. I like to think we have a few bowlers that can present the same challenges," he explained.
Only five runs were added to the overnight 20 for two before Boland struck in his second over of the day.
Debutant Marques Ackerman was caught behind by wicketkeeper Alex Carey for six, with the left-hander edging a ball bowled from around the wicket which seamed away off the pitch.
Matthew Breetzke, who together with Ackerman was brought into the side to strengthen the batting, made only four before he provided Carey with a third catch when he played a loose shot against Starc.

South Africa seemed to be clawing their way back into the contest as Ryan Rickelton (31) added 52 for the fifth wicket with Bavuma but Rickelton fell to a sensational one-handed catch at first slip by Matt Renshaw when Boland was brought back into the attack shortly before the close.
3df04ade1c0f4be5: LONDON, Oct 20 — Selena Gomez has said vaping nicotine has changed her voice, PA Media/dpa reported.
The US singer and actress, 34, told how she has since quit vaping and encouraged others to do the same.
Speaking in an Instagram Stories clip, she said: “I’m not going to be able to change my voice. I vaped nicotine a lot.”
Gomez added: “Nicotine is so hard to quit. I think I just wanted to say if you’re going through it or if you’re even trying to vape, it’s just not worth it. It’s so stupid and it’s changed my voice.
“If you guys don’t like listening to my voice, that’s totally understandable, I don’t mind. Just don’t listen to it.”
Gomez has found staying away from nicotine difficult but encouraged others weaning themselves off it to keep going.
She said: “I am really excited because I stopped and I just hope I can keep it up.
“It’s really hard but I know if you’re going through something, you can get through it too. It sucks.”
Gomez began her career as a child actress on Barney & Friends and later found wider fame on the Disney series Wizards Of Waverly Place (2007-2012).
Her most recent film role was in Emilia Perez (2024) as Jessica Del Monte.
She began her music career in the 2000s and has released three albums with her band, Selena Gomez & The Scene, and three solo albums.
Gomez married music producer Benny Blanco in September 2025.
Gomez has lupus, an autoimmune condition that causes joint pain, skin rashes and tiredness. — Bernama
773c6020d7b35831: From Moaz Nair
Not too long ago, Negeri Sembilan stood proud as a bastion of political tranquillity amidst a turbulent national landscape.

Under the previous Barisan Nasional–Pakatan Harapan coalition government led by former menteri besar Aminuddin Harun, the state enjoyed a rare commodity in modern Malaysian politics: absolute administrative stability.

Today, that hard-won stability has been recklessly squandered. Negeri Sembilan now finds itself ensnared in a historic, multi-layered constitutional crisis born entirely of the current government’s own missteps.

For the voters, legal experts, and everyday citizens witnessing this paralysis, the contrast between past order and present dysfunction could not be starker. The memory of the previous BN-PH framework is fast becoming the definitive benchmark for stable governance and a bitter reminder of how far the state has fallen.

The crowning achievement of the previous administration was its meticulous commitment to preserving constitutional harmony and institutional traditions. Negeri Sembilan’s governance model is uniquely complex, relying on a centuries-old, delicate equilibrium between a modern elected executive, the monarchy, and the state’s sacred, uncodified Adat Perpatih (customary law) institutions.

Aminuddin’s government managed this sensitive balance not by luck, but through sheer political maturity and institutional restraint. Recognising the vital need to insulate daily partisan politics from royal affairs, his government maintained a peaceful, respectful coexistence between elected officials, the Undang Yang Empat (traditional chieftains), and the Yang Dipertuan Besar.
Mutual respect
It was a partnership built on mutual respect and systemic boundaries, ensuring that time-honoured traditions and modern democracy reinforced rather than undermined one another.

Crucially, this political maturity served as a protective shield that insulated the state from systemic crises. Backers of the previous government frequently note that the coalition successfully shielded the civil service and state apparatus from being dragged into protracted constitutional disputes.

Today, we realise just how vital that bulwark was, and how easily it could be dismantled by naked political opportunism. The moment the BN-PH cooperation fractured, it triggered an unprecedented and destructive chain reaction that has shaken the state to its core.

The descent into absolute turmoil accelerated rapidly last April, when 14 BN assemblymen abruptly withdrew their support from Aminuddin’s government following a dispute involving royal affairs. Rather than prioritising state stability, this drastic move plunged the state into a perilous political vacuum, leaving a minority government in its wake and forcing a snap election.

This vacuum did more than just disrupt daily executive governance; it threw open the doors to the current existential crisis— an unprecedented, overt succession dispute between Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir and Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar, who is backed by the current administration.
Constitutional deadlock
The collapse of the foundational political consensus has dragged the state legislative assembly into a complex, multi-layered constitutional deadlock with no clear legal exit ramp.

We are now forced to witness an extraordinary and embarrassing clash of powers. In direct response to aggressive moves by the new state executive council supporting a proclamation to depose him, Tuanku Muhriz took the radical but decisive step of revoking the appointments of all 10 state executive councillors. Citing a direct breach of their oaths of office, the palace purged the state cabinet in one swift stroke.

The fallout has left governance not just shaky, but completely paralysed. The current menteri besar, Ismail Lasim, now stands isolated—a lone captain aboard a ghost ship. In a bizarre attempt to downplay this structural damage, Ismail has chosen to prioritise appointing village chiefs and village development and security committees rather than resolving the critical vacancies in his cabinet.

To claim that state administration is "running smoothly" while the formal sitting of the state assembly has been indefinitely postponed until late November is an insult to the voters' intelligence. This represents a profound failure of the democratic apparatus, where grassroots local appointments are being deployed as a smoke screen to mask a total absence of executive authority.
Painful lesson

Negeri Sembilan is learning a painful lesson first-hand: when you dismantle a functional political consensus for short-term gain, the alternative is rarely better. The current turmoil proves that the previous BN-PH ruling alliance was not merely a marriage of convenience — it was a vital stabilising force.

The current menteri besar cannot continue to govern in a state of absolute paralysis, pretending that village-level appointments can substitute for a functioning state legislative assembly or a complete Exco line-up.

The state’s political leaders must urgently put aside partisan egos, halt their dangerous chess game against traditional institutions, and return to the constitutional blueprint that guaranteed peace for years. The state's executive vacuum is no longer an isolated political squabble; it is a systemic crisis threatening the very fabric of Negeri Sembilan’s unique identity.
If the current leadership is incapable of restoring the stable, respectful equilibrium of the past, they must accept their failure and step aside for those who can.
Moaz Nair is an FMT reader.

49bad1d0fd5314bf: Suatu masa dahulu, tidak terlalu lama berselang, Negeri Sembilan gah berdiri sebagai lambang kestabilan politik yang tenang di tengah-tengah landskap politik nasional yang bergolak.

Di bawah pentadbiran gabungan Barisan Nasional–Pakatan Harapan (BN-PH) terdahulu diterajui bekas menteri besar, Aminuddin Harun, negeri ini mengecapi nikmat yang jarang berlaku dalam politik Malaysia moden: kestabilan pentadbiran yang mutlak.
Hari ini, kestabilan yang sukar dibina itu telah dipertaruhkan dengan begitu rakus.
Negeri Sembilan kini terperangkap dalam krisis perlembagaan bersejarah yang berlapis-lapis, cetusan daripada kesilapan kerajaan sekarang sendiri.
Bagi pengundi, pakar undang-undang dan marhaen yang menyaksikan kelumpuhan ini, jurang perbezaan antara ketenteraman lalu dengan kepincangan sekarang amatlah ketara.
Memori kerangka kerja BN-PH terdahulu dengan pantas menjadi penanda aras utama tadbir urus yang stabil—sekali gus menjadi peringatan pahit tentang betapa parahnya kejatuhan negeri ini sekarang.
Pencapaian terbesar pentadbiran terdahulu adalah ketelitian dan kesungguhannya dalam memelihara keharmonian perlembagaan serta tradisi.

Model tadbir urus Negeri Sembilan memiliki keunikan yang kompleks; ia bergantung kepada keseimbangan rapuh berusia berabad-abad lamanya antara cabang eksekutif moden yang dipilih dengan institusi beraja serta institusi Adat Perpatih negeri yang sakral lagi tidak berkod.
Kerajaan pimpinan Aminuddin berjaya mengemudi keseimbangan sensitif ini bukan atas faktor tuah, sebaliknya melalui kematangan politik yang jitu dan kawalan diri institusional.

Dengan menyedari keperluan untuk mengasingkan pergolakan politik kepartian harian daripada urusan diraja, pentadbiran terdahulu berjaya mengekalkan kebersamaan yang aman lagi hormat-menghormati antara wakil rakyat dipilih, Undang Yang Empat dan Yang Dipertuan Besar.
Ia merupakan perkongsian yang dibina atas asas saling menghormati dan sempadan sistemik, bagi memastikan tradisi zaman-berzaman dan demokrasi moden saling memperkukuh, bukannya saling meruntuhkan.
Apa yang penting, kematangan politik ini berfungsi sebagai perisai pelindung yang menyelamatkan negeri daripada krisis sistemik.
Penyokong pentadbiran lalu sering menegaskan bahawa pakatan tersebut berjaya melindungi perkhidmatan awam dan jentera kerajaan daripada heretan pertikaian perlembagaan yang berlarutan.
Kini kita menyedari betapa pentingnya benteng perlindungan tersebut, dan betapa mudahnya ia dihancurkan oleh oportunisme politik yang melampau.
Detik runtuhnya kerjasama BN-PH telah mencetuskan tindak balas berantai yang merosakkan dan belum pernah terjadi sebelum ini, sekali gus menggoncang segenap sanubari negeri.
Kejatuhan ke kancah pergolakan mutlak ini memecut pantas pada April lalu, apabila 14 Adun BN bertindak menarik balik sokongan secara mengejut ekoran perselisihan faham berkaitan isu diraja.
Alih-alih mengutamakan kestabilan negeri, tindakan drastik ini telah menghumban negeri ke dalam vakum politik yang berbahaya, meninggalkan kerajaan minoriti dan memaksa pilihan raya kilat diadakan.

Vakum ini bukan sahaja mengganggu tadbir urus eksekutif harian, malah membuka seluas-luasnya pintu kepada krisis eksistensial semasa—pertikaian terbuka mengenai takhta yang tidak pernah berlaku sebelum ini antara Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir dan Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja'afar yang disokong pihak pentadbiran.
Runtuhnya konsensus politik asas tersebut telah mengheret DUN ke dalam kebuntuan perlembagaan yang amat rumit dan berlapis, tanpa sebarang jalan keluar undang-undang yang jelas.
Kita kini terpaksa menyaksikan pertembungan kuasa yang luar biasa dan memalukan.

Sebagai tindak balas langsung terhadap tindakan agresif ahli Majlis Mesyuarat Kerajaan Negeri yang baharu menyokong proklamasi untuk menyingkirkan baginda, Tuanku Muhriz telah mengambil langkah radikal namun tegas dengan membatalkan pelantikan semua 10 exco.
Pihak istana menyatakan sebab pelanggaran sumpah jawatan secara langsung, sekali gus membersihkan kabinet negeri dalam satu tindakan drastik.
Impak daripada senario ini menyaksikan tadbir urus bukan sekadar goyah—tetapi lumpuh sepenuhnya.
Menteri besar semasa, Ismail Lasim, kini berdiri sebatang kara, bertindak bagaikan kapten tunggal di atas kapal berhantu.

Dalam cubaan aneh untuk memperkecilkan impak kerosakan struktur ini, Ismail memilih untuk mengutamakan pelantikan ketua-ketua kampung dan Jawatankuasa Pembangunan dan Keselamatan Kampung (JPKK) berbanding menyelesaikan kekosongan kritikal dalam kabinetnya.
Dakwaan bahawa pentadbiran negeri 'berjalan lancar' sedangkan sidang rasmi DUN telah ditangguhkan tanpa tarikh pasti sehingga akhir November adalah satu penghinaan kepada kebijaksanaan pengundi.
Ini adalah kegagalan besar dalam radas demokrasi, di mana pelantikan peringkat akar umbi tempatan digunakan sebagai tirai asap untuk menutup ketiadaan kuasa eksekutif yang menyeluruh.

Negeri Sembilan kini sedang mempelajari pengajaran yang perit secara langsung: apabila anda merombak konsensus politik yang berfungsi demi keuntungan jangka pendek, alternatifnya jarang sekali menjadi lebih baik.
Pergolakan semasa membuktikan bahawa pakatan pemerintah BN-PH terdahulu bukan sekadar perkahwinan politik atas dasar kepentingan—ia adalah kuasa penstabil yang amat penting.

Pentadbiran semasa tidak boleh terus memerintah dalam keadaan lumpuh mutlak, sambil berpura-pura bahawa pelantikan di peringkat kampung boleh menggantikan DUN yang berfungsi atau barisan exco yang lengkap.

Pemimpin politik di negeri ini mesti segera mengetepikan ego kepartian, menghentikan permainan catur yang berbahaya terhadap institusi tradisi negeri dan kembali kepada pelan tindakan perlembagaan yang telah menjamin keamanan selama bertahun-tahun.
Vakum eksekutif negeri ini bukan lagi sekadar pertikaian politik yang terpencil; ia adalah krisis sistemik yang mengancam struktur identiti unik Negeri Sembilan.

Jika kepimpinan sedia ada tidak mampu memulihkan keseimbangan yang stabil dan saling menghormati seperti masa lalu, mereka harus menerima hakikat kegagalan mereka dan berundur demi memberi laluan kepada mereka yang mampu.

658806b05c2392d3: PETALING JAYA: Long before betel nut was served from ornate trays at Malay weddings or offered to guests as a gesture of hospitality, people in this part of the world may already have been seeking out its stimulating effects.

Recent research published in "Science Advances" has found evidence that hunter-gatherers in Sulawesi, Indonesia, were habitually using betel nut as far back as 25,000 years ago. The findings push the known history of psychoactive plant use far deeper into the prehistoric past than researchers had previously been able to demonstrate.
The study examined the remains of two pre-agricultural individuals from caves in South Sulawesi, one dating to between 25,000 and 16,000 years ago and the other to between 7,600 and 6,300 years ago.
Both had unusual rounded grooves worn into their molars, suggesting that hard objects had repeatedly been held against their teeth over long periods.

Biomolecular analysis of the teeth also produced evidence consistent with exposure to betel nut. According to the researchers, the most likely explanation is that these ancient foragers repeatedly sucked whole areca nuts rather than chewing the prepared betel quid more familiar today.

The areca nut contains arecoline, a stimulant that can produce heightened alertness and mild euphoria. Experiments carried out as part of the study showed that simply keeping a whole nut in the mouth for prolonged periods can release the compound, even without the slaked lime commonly used in later betel-chewing traditions.

Researchers say the practice may initially have had a practical purpose. Betel nut can numb the mouth, raising the possibility that people sucked it to relieve dental pain, although its stimulant effects may also have encouraged repeated use.

What the findings do not show is that people 25,000 years ago were chewing sirih pinang exactly as Malaysians would recognise it. The familiar quid of betel leaf, areca nut and slaked lime appears to have developed later, and precisely when that combination emerged remains uncertain.

By historical times, however, betel chewing had become deeply embedded across Southeast Asia. In the Malay world, "makan sirih" or "menginang" was not merely a personal habit but part of hospitality, courtship, weddings and ceremonial exchange.

According to Badan Warisan Malaysia, the basic Malay betel quid traditionally combined betel leaf, lime and slices of areca nut, often with gambir added as a fourth ingredient. Tobacco and spices could also be included depending on taste and local custom.

The practice also gave rise to an entire material culture. Ingredients were stored and presented in "tepak sirih" or betel boxes made from materials ranging from wood and brass to silver and gold, some of them elaborate enough to become treasured household or ceremonial objects.

Across the wider region, offering betel once functioned as an important social ritual. Historical accounts describe it as common in Malay, Indian and Peranakan households, where sharing a quid could signal welcome, respect or sociability

In Malaysia, betel chewing is far less common today than it once was, particularly among younger generations. Yet its traces remain visible in language, wedding customs, museum collections and surviving tepak sirih sets that recall a time when offering betel was almost as much about manners as appetite.
The new Sulawesi discovery does not prove a direct cultural line stretching unbroken from Ice Age foragers to modern Malaysian traditions.

But what it does suggest is that long before silver betel boxes, wedding ceremonies and carefully folded leaves, somebody in prehistoric Southeast Asia was already reaching for an areca nut - and apparently doing so often enough to leave the evidence behind in their teeth.
0a3466dddd7a903a: PARIS, France: Next week the winner of the most prestigious individual award in football will be announced at the Ballon d'Or ceremony in London, and some of the leading contenders for the prize will be on the same pitch on Tuesday when Paris Saint-Germain host Barcelona in the UEFA Champions League.
In the home camp, there is a remarkable total of 10 players among the 30 nominees, including last year's laureate Ousmane Dembele.

Facing up to them, Barcelona have three of their own candidates, with last year's runner-up Lamine Yamal and 2024 winner Rodri along with defender Pau Cubarsi, another member of Spain's triumphant World Cup side.

The battle for the Ballon d'Or gives an edge to this game that might otherwise be lacking, given the relatively limited stakes for these two powerhouses in the new league phase format of Europe's elite club competition.

The individual prize to recognise the standout player of each season does not carry the same weight or significance everywhere, but it is a major talking point in France – it was created by France Football magazine in the 1950s – and in Spain where Barcelona and Real Madrid campaign loudly for their candidates.
In Madrid they are backing Kylian Mbappe. He has been making his own case in public, as has Yamal, the 19-year-old winger who starred as Barcelona won La Liga and then won the World Cup with Spain.
"I think all those who watch football understand the argument in my favour. I go out onto the pitch, I have fun, and I play well," Yamal told French sports daily L'Equipe recently.
"Fortunately I have also won a lot of titles with Barca and in addition to that I won the most important title of all, the World Cup.
"But beyond that I think my way of playing is my strongest argument and what makes me different."

The voting by a jury of journalists from the top 100 countries in the FIFA rankings is only based on last season, but Yamal has already made a formidable start to this campaign and scored a stunning goal in Barcelona's 5-2 weekend win at Betis in La Liga.
Not that PSG, who are going for a third consecutive Champions League title this season, are scared of him.
"I wouldn't say we are afraid," insisted PSG midfielder Vitinha on Monday.

"He is one of the best players in the world. What he does is incredible. He is exceptional. It is always interesting to play against these types of players, but not just him. We are facing a great team, not only Lamine."
NO OBVIOUS CANDIDATE?
Vitinha, the 26-year-old Portuguese playmaker, came third in the 2025 Ballon d'Or ranking.
Dembele won it last year off the back of an extraordinary season in which he scored 35 goals in all competitions and helped inspire PSG to their first ever Champions League title.

Last season was less exceptional, even if he still found the net 20 times including in the Champions League final against Arsenal, and the 29-year-old France star has been making his case in the media too.
"I have never been the chosen one, but I worked hard and last year I was rewarded for a fantastic year," he said in response to comments by Mbappe in relation to the Ballon d'Or.
"This year we will see, but there is no pressure. I'm easy."
PSG might be the outstanding club team just now, but their problem could be the lack of one obvious candidate.
Khvicha Kvaratskhelia was surely the best player in last season's Champions League, but the Georgian winger did not go to the World Cup.
Fabian Ruiz is in the unique position of having won the Champions League and World Cup, but lacks the real superstar pedigree.
Ferran Torres swapped Barca for PSG after scoring the only goal in the World Cup final, yet is not seen as a realistic Ballon d'Or winner.
"I have big respect for both Kylian and Yamal. They are amazing players," said PSG president Nasser al-Khelaifi recently.
"But I would go for sure for my players. We have three players: Dembele, 'Kvara' and also Fabian Ruiz, who is the only one to have won all the trophies. They deserve it."
