9f886b38af62809a: WASHINGTON: The World Bank on Monday announced a new strategy aimed at boosting connectivity and making digital access more affordable in developing countries.
"Digital technology can help countries create jobs and make scarce resources go further," said World Bank president Ajay Banga.
"Realising that potential requires a comprehensive approach – from reliable connectivity and affordable devices to digital skills and useful services," he added in a statement.
Developing countries face a crunch with limited resources and a rising need for employment, the Washington-headquartered institution said.
While 1.2 billion people are set to reach working age in such countries over the next 10-15 years, these economies are projected to create just 420 million or so jobs.
The bank's strategy aims to support infrastructure for connectivity and lower the cost of entry-level smartphone and broadband services.
It also wants to widen access to digital services and look into targeted uses of artificial intelligence.
The bank said only 23% of people in low-income countries used the Internet, a stark contrast against 94% in high-income countries.
1e6aae27ee385fbf: NEW YORK: Veteran journalist Christiane Amanpour said on Monday that she was leaving her role at CNN after a 43-year career as one of the US broadcaster's most prominent international correspondents.
"After thinking carefully for several months and experiencing a few sleepless nights, as you can imagine, I've decided to separate from CNN," Amanpour, 68, said in a statement.
Her announcement came weeks after media corporation Paramount Skydance formally took over Warner Bros. Discovery, the parent company of CNN.
The merger has raised concerns over CNN's independence, as the merged company's owners, the Ellison family, are close allies of US President Donald Trump — a fierce critic of the television network.
Amanpour did not reference the deal but emphasised her commitment to being "fiercely independent".
"That's especially important today as we face unprecedented pressures from all sides, political, financial, and also from the rising dangers in the field," she said.
British-born Amanpour first became known to CNN's international audience for her coverage of the 1991 Gulf War, which followed Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
She has interviewed many of the world's leaders and newsmakers over the past decades and reported from hotspots such as Iraq, Afghanistan, Pakistan, Somalia, Rwanda and the Balkans.
Amanpour said her daily news show on CNN would be scaled back to once a week until next June, while her PBS programme would also end.

She added that she "looks forward to interesting new projects down the line, and will always be rooting for CNN and maintaining its history of independent journalism. Remember: always be truthful, not neutral."
In a memo carried by US media, CNN chief executive Mark Thompson praised Amanpour "for 43 extraordinary years of remarkable journalism, loyalty and friendship".
"Like so many CNNers who will hear the news today, I'm very sorry to see her go, but I've come to accept that this is the right time for her, both personally and professionally," Thompson said.
02a1f726a223648e: WASHINGTON: US president Donald Trump used the protests roiling France to score some quick political points Monday, as the upcoming midterm elections force his Republican party to face strong headwinds.

While speaking with reporters Trump recalled an exchange with his French counterpart Emmanuel Macron: "I told him a long time ago, you're making a big mistake in France. You're letting everybody from the world come in...Paris is going to be a Muslim city very soon."
Earlier Monday, the 80-year-old president wrote on his Truth Social platform: "The migrants have taken over France. They must CLOSE THE BORDERS, FAST!"
Cost-of-living demonstrations broke out across France over the weekend, with many devolving into looting and violent conflict, prompting officials to institute partial curfews Monday.

While the French protests were inspired by soaring inflation, Trump has molded the violent clashes with police into evidence in favor of the anti-immigration policies he used to successfully campaign for reelection in 2024.
"They're taking this French crisis and turning it into a campaign argument," JC Lintzenich, a senior fellow with the German Marshall Fund think tank, told AFP.
Conservative talking points
Opinion polls heavily favour Trump's rival Democratic Party in the No 3 midterm elections, which will determine who will take control of Congress.
With just two weeks to go before Americans go to the polls, Trump has grasped any strategy he can to compel voters to support the Republican party and his Make America Great Again (MAGA) movement.

"Since the beginning of the MAGA movement, Europe has been an extension of the US political battlefield, so it's not surprising that when there are events like the unrest from Oct 17, the political machine gets moving," Justin Vaisse, a professor of US foreign policy at Johns Hopkins University, told AFP.

As videos of France's unrest began surfacing on social media, Trump's vice president JD Vance wrote Saturday on X: "Western liberals imported the third world into France... they ignored fundamental questions of assimilation and compatibility."

Right-wing US media personalities, including Glenn Beck, Benny Johnson, Nick Sortor and Jack Posobiec made similar points, blaming immigrants from Muslim-majority countries for causing a crisis in Western identity.
"The riots are viewed as validation of the warnings against immigration in general and Muslim immigration, if such a thing exists," Vaisse said.

Celia Belin, a senior policy fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations and head of its Paris office, views the commentary as an "export of domestic policies" from a US administration that openly supports nationalist parties in Europe.

She told AFP that Trump and his allies "rushed into this argument, the same one that Vance had presented in Munich" in 2025, in a controversial speech described as a US culture war against Europe, with the goal of "fanning the flames."
Polling priorities
Experts note that this rhetorical strategy, while it may have succeeded in 2024, is not necessarily what US voters want to hear these days.
"When you look at the campaign ads here - I'm in South Carolina right now - it's about healthcare, domestic issues," Lintzenich said.
"The international element is a blip on the radar, and Ukraine, and Iran, and other ongoing national security issues rate higher than the current French instability," he continued.
A Pew Research poll this month found the economy plays an important role in the choice of 82% of US voters, a far higher number than immigration (59%) or race-related issues (36%).

Though Trump has followed through on his 2024 campaign promise to crack down on immigration, he has fared less successfully on his other promise to tamp down on inflation, with his tariff policies and war with Iran spiking prices across the economy, plunging his approval rating to record lows.
Vaisse said using linking US identitarian rhetoric with the events in France "is not going to win a single vote" for Republicans, though it could "mobilise the base" to vote.

5771bdd27f737e08: KYIV: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused the United States on Monday of deliberately delaying the delivery of interceptor missiles to his country, as tensions between Kyiv and Washington escalated over military aid and intelligence-sharing.
Kyiv said it had received no early warning of powerful Russian missile strikes, echoing similar claims made last week.

Speaking to US senators on Monday, Zelenskyy said "the Pentagon is delaying the delivery of missiles" already paid for by European countries, and that the shipment was awaiting US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth's signature.
He also said several European countries were ready to transfer Patriot interceptor missiles from their own stockpiles but were still awaiting US approval.
"The missiles are ready, and they could already be in Ukraine," Zelenskyy said. "But unfortunately, there is still no approval."
The United States has denied making any changes to intelligence-sharing with Ukraine.

Trump has also denied ordering a reduction in speeds on the US government-owned and -controlled Starshield network after Elon Musk, whose company SpaceX developed it, said the order could only have come from the White House.
Strained relations

Relations between the two capitals have been strained since Trump partially lifted sanctions to strike a diesel supply deal with Vladimir Putin and slammed Zelenskyy as a warmonger over Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries.
On Monday, Trump defended the diesel deal while once again criticising Zelenskyy.
"Zelenskyy doesn't know what he's talking about," Trump said. "To be honest, I think it's time for somebody else to negotiate on behalf of Ukraine."

Trump also said he was ready to meet Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in China next month to discuss denuclearisation, adding that the talks could also cover the war in Ukraine — fuelling fears in Kyiv that it was being sidelined.

Earlier in Moscow, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said "the topic of such a hypothetical has indeed been mentioned" when asked about a Wall Street Journal report on Sunday that Trump, Putin and Xi could meet.
Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiga said such a meeting would "only encourage Putin to continue this war".
Meanwhile, Zelenskyy also spoke to Pope Leo XIV on Monday, according to the Vatican, days after the Catholic leader held a similar call with Putin.
The Vatican said the Pope had urged both sides to allow aid to flow into the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky and civilians to leave.
No information on latest strikes
Russia's latest strikes again hit Ukrainian energy facilities and infrastructure across the country, cutting power to more than 500,000 people and forcing emergency repairs to the battered grid.
"Once again, there was no early warning from our partners," Zelenskyy said as he detailed the damage, deaths and injuries.
Six people, including three children, were killed in a strike near the northeastern city of Kharkiv, the authorities said.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, visiting Uzbekistan on Monday, denied that intelligence-sharing with Ukraine had been withdrawn, backing Trump's call for Zelenskyy to focus on ending the conflict.

Talks to end Europe's deadliest conflict since World War II remain deadlocked, with Russia refusing to give up its claim to Ukrainian territory and Ukraine steadfastly rejecting attempts to force it to do so.
Trump had vowed to end the war swiftly when he returned to office but has since appeared to tilt towards Russia, including by calling for Zelenskyy to be replaced.

9feff5399421f02f: KUALA LUMPUR: Sports critic Zakaria Rahim is asking a question that many football fans are asking — how did the FA of Malaysia (FAM) get shortlisted for the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) Member Association of the Year 2026 Gold category award after all the controversies?
"How can an association facing such governance troubles, as highlighted during the EGM (last month) be among the three potential award recipients?" Zakaria asked.

As things stand, questions over transparency at FAM have intensified amid the delays in releasing details of the AFC audit and the Court of Arbitration for Sport's (CAS) "reasoned grounds" on the case of the seven suspended heritage players.
A CAS offcial told Timesport last month that the full arbitral award was expected before the end of last month. However, till now it is yet to be made known publicly.

Meanwhile, the full report of the AFC audit remains undisclosed. Earlier this year, the Asian body carried out a four-month governance and financial audit of FAM following the naturalised players scandal which led to sanctions by FIFA against FAM.

AFC general-secretary Datuk Seri Windsor Paul said in March: "We will certainly present some findings to the public. We want to be transparent. However, the full report will first go to FAM, and it will then decide if it wants to make the full findings available."
Windsor also said last month that the complete document would be presented to FAM's new executive committee.
The preliminary findings presented by AFC deputy general-secretary Vahid Kardany during FAM's Extraordinary Congress showed serious structural weaknesses.

"What we are seeing is a chronic condition across the organisation. The problems are not confined to one area but are recurring across the entire structure, pointing to systemic weaknesses in governance, accountability and institutional design," Vahid reportedly said in June.
He also noted that formal governance structures had not been rigorously enforced, resulting in informal concentrations of authority and a culture in which staff hesitated to raise concerns.
Zakaria warned that withholding the CAS report and full AFC audit could deepen public mistrust in FAM.
"As far as I remember, when CAS issued the operative award, it indicated that the full judgment would follow.
"I am of the view that if the full judgment is made public, more uncomfortable details will emerge. I hope the FAM Integrity Committee proves me wrong by publishing the judgment," said Zakaria.
Timesport has contacted FAM for clarification, but has yet to receive a response.
b74a16464541cb3a: PETALING JAYA: The resignations of two Gerakan leaders in Penang have highlighted discontent over the party’s alliance with PAS and concerns about its leadership, analysts say.
Ahmad Fauzi Abdul Hamid of Universiti Sains Malaysia said some members were unhappy with Gerakan’s apparent shift to the right.

“Some leaders, both young and old, appear to think that Perikatan Nasional, since its leadership was taken over by PAS and Bersatu was weakened, has shown theocratic tendencies that are ultimately at odds with Gerakan’s secular character,” he told FMT.

Lau Zhe Wei of the International Islamic University Malaysia said some members were uncomfortable with what they saw as Gerakan’s subservience to PAS, which leads PN. However, some former Gerakan members had joined Wawasan and the PAS non-Muslim wing.

“I would not say those who resigned are necessarily uncomfortable with PAS, because they might eventually join another party associated with PAS. One thing is certain: Gerakan no longer seems able to attract or retain many leaders, or even members,” he said.

On Sept 6, Penang Gerakan Youth chief Tan Zhen Zune resigned from his youth wing position as well as party deputy secretary-general, citing dissatisfaction with the leadership and decisions he said had compromised the party’s principles. He remains a party member.

The New Straits Times reported that Tan had repeatedly raised his concerns with the leadership. He said his objection was not to working with PAS or Umno, but to doing so at the expense of Gerakan’s principles. He also cited statements by PAS that he considered extreme.

Three days later, former Gerakan national treasurer H’ng Chee Wey resigned after 31 years with the party. He did not disclose his reasons but posted a cryptic message on Facebook, saying that while political differences were normal in a democracy, “there is no need to become sworn enemies, nor is there any need to attack each other or even turn against each other”.
At odds with party leadership

A Gerakan insider told FMT that the resignations reflected some dissatisfaction with party president Dominic Lau’s push for closer ties with PAS which the source said "does not treat us as an ally and always attacks our president. They don’t respect Gerakan”.
“But whenever they need votes PAS will come to us and other PN component parties. We don’t want to be a second fiddle within PN. This is why members in Penang are dissatisfied.”
Tensions between Dominic and PAS leaders have surfaced before. In August 2023, Dominic was chased away from a PAS ceramah in Tasek Gelugor by a state party leader.

Penang PAS leaders also objected to Dominic contesting the Bayan Lepas seat in the 2023 state election. He came under criticism at the PAS general assembly in 2025, prompting PAS secretary-general Takiyuddin Hassan and vice-president Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar to apologise.

However, the insider said some Gerakan members, particularly in Kedah, wanted the alliance to continue. The source said the partnership could help Gerakan contest mixed seats held by PKR and Barisan Nasional, amid shifting political alliances, including cooperation between PN parties and BN in Negeri Sembilan.
Not a sign of wider revolt

Fauzi said the resignations did not necessarily signal a wider revolt against Gerakan’s membership in PN, noting that Tan had retained his party membership. Instead, he said, they could prompt discussions about Gerakan’s future as a multiracial party.
“There is still broad agreement with the party’s principles, but concerns about its future are being openly expressed. If the current leadership does not take precautions, the situation could worsen.

“Discontented members hope the resignations will trigger further internal deliberations, making the grassroots aware of any changes to the party’s ideological direction and what these mean for its response to issues,” he said.
Zhe Wei said the resignations also reflected grassroots anger over what members saw as PAS’s mistreatment and marginalisation of Gerakan.

He cited the appointment of a PAS member as village chief of a Chinese new village in Negeri Sembilan, a position he said could have gone to Gerakan. He also pointed to Penang PAS’s objections to Dominic contesting the Bayan Lepas seat.
Gerakan urged to rethink role
Zhe Wei said Gerakan should reconsider its membership in PN, noting that it had failed to win more seats despite the coalition’s gains in recent elections.
“Why not leave PN and stand on its own, or join Bersatu? Who knows, perhaps Gerakan could gain support 10 years down the road,” he said, referring to divisions between Bersatu and PAS within PN.

“Maybe it will not gain support either. But compared with staying in PN and putting up with PAS’s current treatment of Gerakan, I think it is worth taking the risk of leaving the coalition,” he added.

Fauzi said Gerakan could not blame PAS or PN for its electoral difficulties. Instead, it needed to reassess its policies and positions, given its failure to win non-Malay voters from Pakatan Harapan, particularly DAP.

“If PN’s true colours are increasingly being exposed through PAS’s allegedly extreme positions, Gerakan must decide whether to stay. If it wants to remain, it may have to change some of its hardline secularist positions, which could ultimately bring it into conflict with PAS.
“But that risks unrest among ideological hardliners in the party who would oppose what they see as an abandonment of its cherished principles. Nobody is forcing Gerakan to stay in PN,” he said.
8eb8a9c413244d24: PETALING JAYA: Peletakan jawatan dua pemimpin Gerakan di Pulau Pinang menyerlahkan rasa tidak puas hati terhadap kerjasama parti itu dengan PAS serta kebimbangan mengenai kepimpinannya, menurut penganalisis.
Ahmad Fauzi Abdul Hamid dari Universiti Sains Malaysia berkata sebahagian ahli tidak berpuas hati dengan kecenderungan Gerakan yang dilihat semakin ke kanan.

“Sesetengah pemimpin, baik muda mahupun veteran, nampaknya merasakan Perikatan Nasional (PN), sejak kepimpinannya diambil alih PAS dan Bersatu, ia menjadi semakin lemah, menunjukkan kecenderungan teokratik yang akhirnya bercanggah dengan sifat sekular Gerakan,” katanya kepada FMT.

Lau Zhe Wei dari Universiti Islam Antarabangsa Malaysia berkata sebahagian ahli tidak selesa dengan apa yang mereka anggap sebagai sikap Gerakan yang terlalu tunduk kepada PAS, parti yang menerajui PN. Bagaimanapun, beberapa bekas ahli Gerakan telah menyertai Wawasan dan sayap bukan Islam PAS.

“Saya tidak akan mengatakan mereka yang meletak jawatan semestinya tidak selesa dengan PAS kerana mereka mungkin akhirnya menyertai parti lain yang mempunyai kaitan dengan PAS. Satu perkara yang pasti, Gerakan nampaknya tidak lagi mampu menarik atau mengekalkan ramai pemimpin mahupun ahli,” katanya.

Pada 6 Sept, Ketua Pemuda Gerakan Pulau Pinang Tan Zhen Zune meletak jawatan dalam sayap pemuda serta jawatan timbalan setiausaha agung parti, dengan alasan tidak berpuas hati terhadap kepimpinan dan keputusan yang menurutnya telah mengkompromikan prinsip parti. Beliau kekal sebagai ahli parti.

New Straits Times melaporkan, Tan berulang kali membangkitkan kebimbangannya kepada kepimpinan parti. Beliau berkata bantahannya bukan terhadap kerjasama dengan PAS atau Umno, tetapi terhadap tindakan berbuat demikian sehingga mengorbankan prinsip Gerakan. Beliau turut memetik kenyataan PAS yang dianggapnya melampau.
Tiga hari kemudian, bekas bendahari agung Gerakan H’ng Chee Wey meletak jawatan selepas 31 tahun bersama parti itu.

Beliau tidak mendedahkan sebab peletakan jawatannya, sebaliknya memuat naik hantaran berkias di Facebook dengan menyatakan bahawa meskipun perbezaan politik perkara biasa dalam demokrasi tetapi 'tidak perlu menjadi musuh ketat, apatah lagi menyerang atau bermusuhan sesama sendiri'.
Bercanggah dengan kepimpinan parti

Seorang sumber dalaman Gerakan memberitahu FMT, peletakan jawatan itu mencerminkan rasa tidak puas hati sebahagian pihak terhadap usaha Presiden Gerakan Dominic Lau untuk menjalinkan hubungan lebih rapat dengan PAS.
Sumber itu berkata PAS 'tidak menganggap kita sebagai sekutu dan sentiasa menyerang presiden. Mereka tidak menghormati Gerakan”.

“Namun, setiap kali mereka memerlukan undi, PAS akan datang kepada kami dan parti komponen PN yang lain. Kami tidak mahu menjadi pihak kelas kedua dalam PN. Sebab itulah ahli di Pulau Pinang tidak berpuas hati,” katanya.
Ketegangan antara Lau dengan pemimpin PAS pernah tercetus sebelum ini. Pada Ogos 2023, Lau dihalau keluar dari ceramah PAS di Tasek Gelugor oleh seorang pemimpin parti itu di peringkat negeri.

Pemimpin PAS Pulau Pinang turut membantah keputusan Lau bertanding di kerusi Bayan Lepas pada PRN 2023. Beliau juga dikritik pada Muktamar PAS 2025, sehingga mendorong Setiausaha Agung PAS Takiyuddin Hassan dan Naib Presidennya Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar memohon maaf.
Bagaimanapun, sumber dalaman itu berkata sebahagian ahli Gerakan, khususnya di Kedah, mahu kerjasama tersebut diteruskan.

Menurut sumber itu, kerjasama berkenaan boleh membantu Gerakan bertanding di kerusi campuran yang dipegang PKR dan Barisan Nasional (BN), ketika landskap kerjasama politik terus berubah, termasuk kerjasama antara parti PN dengan BN di Negeri Sembilan.
Bukan petanda tentangan lebih meluas

Fauzi berkata peletakan jawatan itu tidak semestinya menandakan penentangan lebih meluas terhadap penyertaan Gerakan dalam PN, sambil menyatakan bahawa Tan masih kekal sebagai ahli parti. Sebaliknya, beliau berkata perkembangan itu boleh mencetuskan perbincangan mengenai masa depan Gerakan sebagai parti berbilang kaum.

“Masih terdapat kesepakatan umum terhadap prinsip parti, tetapi kebimbangan mengenai masa depannya disuarakan secara terbuka. Jika kepimpinan semasa tidak mengambil langkah berjaga-jaga, keadaan boleh menjadi lebih buruk.

“Ahli yang tidak berpuas hati berharap peletakan jawatan itu akan mencetuskan perbincangan dalaman lanjut, sekali gus menyedarkan akar umbi tentang sebarang perubahan hala tuju ideologi parti dan implikasinya terhadap pendirian parti dalam menangani pelbagai isu,” katanya.
Lau berkata peletakan jawatan itu turut mencerminkan kemarahan akar umbi terhadap apa yang dianggap oleh ahli sebagai layanan buruk PAS terhadap Gerakan serta tindakan meminggirkan parti itu.

Beliau memberikan contoh pelantikan seorang ahli PAS sebagai ketua kampung di sebuah kampung baru Cina di Negeri Sembilan, jawatan yang menurutnya boleh diberikan kepada Gerakan. Beliau turut merujuk bantahan PAS Pulau Pinang terhadap tindakan Lau bertanding di kerusi Bayan Lepas.
Gerakan digesa nilai semula peranan

Lau berkata Gerakan perlu mempertimbangkan semula keanggotaannya dalam PN, sambil menyatakan parti itu gagal memenangi lebih banyak kerusi meskipun gabungan berkenaan mencatatkan kemajuan dalam pilihan raya baru-baru ini.

“Mengapa tidak keluar daripada PN dan bergerak sendiri, atau menyertai Bersatu? Siapa tahu, mungkin Gerakan boleh meraih sokongan dalam tempoh 10 tahun akan datang,” katanya, merujuk kepada perpecahan antara Bersatu dengan PAS dalam PN.

“Mungkin parti itu juga tidak akan mendapat sokongan. Namun, berbanding terus kekal dalam PN dan menerima layanan PAS terhadap Gerakan ketika ini, saya fikir risiko meninggalkan gabungan itu berbaloi untuk diambil,” tambahnya.

Fauzi berkata Gerakan tidak boleh menyalahkan PAS atau PN atas masalah yang dihadapinya dalam pilihan raya. Sebaliknya, parti itu perlu menilai semula dasar dan pendiriannya susulan kegagalannya menarik pengundi bukan Melayu daripada Pakatan Harapan (PH), khususnya DAP.

“Jika wajah sebenar PN semakin terserlah menerusi pendirian PAS yang didakwa ekstrem, Gerakan mesti memutuskan sama ada mahu terus kekal. Jika mahu kekal, parti itu mungkin perlu mengubah beberapa pendirian sekularnya yang tegas, sekali gus berisiko mencetuskan konflik dengan PAS.

“Namun, langkah itu boleh mencetuskan ketidakpuasan hati dalam kalangan anggota parti yang berpegang teguh pada ideologi dan menentang apa yang mereka anggap sebagai pengabaian prinsip yang selama ini dipertahankan. Tiada siapa memaksa Gerakan untuk kekal dalam PN,” katanya.
b26547cd41e70171: KUALA LUMPUR: Your body works hard to keep your vital organs at the ideal temperature. But sometimes your hands and feet get left out in the cold, so to speak.
While it's perfectly normal for fingers and toes to feel chilly from time to time, especially in cool weather, constantly cold extremities may signal that your health deserves a closer look.

“Two of the most common reasons for cold hands and feet are stress and anxiety. That’s completely normal. But there are certain medical conditions as well which may cause that, such as diabetes, high cholesterol or thyroid disorders,” pharmacist Benjamin Lim told FMT Lifestyle.
“If you are experiencing cold hands and feet on a long-term basis, or if it keeps getting worse, you may want to get checked to make sure there are no underlying problems.”

One possible cause is poor blood circulation. According to Lim, cold hands and feet accompanied by symptoms such as fatigue, difficulty concentrating, ringing in the ears, or pain while walking could indicate an underlying circulatory problem.

He warned, however, that patients should first seek medical advice to determine whether their cold hands and feet are caused by an underlying health condition, rather than attempting to self-diagnose.

Lim explained that healthy blood circulation is essential for delivering oxygen and nutrients to every part of the body. When blood circulation is impaired, nerves and tissues may not receive an adequate supply, resulting in numbness, tingling or coldness in the hands and feet.

“Even though the brain occupies only 2% of our body weight, it uses 20% of our body’s oxygen and energy. It is very sensitive to problems of poor blood circulation, which can affect eye health and wound healing,” he said.
University of Malaya Professor of Geriatric Medicine Prof Dr Tan Maw Pin elaborated that this phenomenon is caused by blood vessels constricting to retain heat.

“You’re not getting enough blood supply to your peripheries, or the outer parts of the body. The body reduces blood flow there to ensure enough blood goes to vital organs such as the brain and heart,” she said.

Meanwhile, Lim added that scientific research shows lack of sleep, mild dehydration, or an extremely sedentary lifestyle often contribute to impaired blood circulation. Stress could also lead to anxiety, which in turn causes blood vessels to constrict, thereby aggravating this problem.
Adequate and consistent physical activity is, therefore, important for everyone, especially knowledge workers and professionals, to help relax the body and promote blood flow.
“If you find yourself sitting for a long time, you should get up from time to time and move for about five minutes every hour, at least,” Lim said.

He noted that certain supplements, such as ginkgo biloba, may help support healthy blood circulation. The herb contains antioxidant compounds and is believed to promote blood flow by improving circulation.

For example, the body’s endothelium - a continuous layer of specialised cells lining the interior surface of blood vessels, lymphatic vessels and heart chambers - often releases nitric oxide. This helps dilate blood vessels.

However, this chemical breaks down easily due to oxidative stress. Lim elaborated that gingko biloba helps slow down this process, ensuring more nitric oxide remains available to relax blood vessels, thereby promoting healthier blood flow.

Overall, while an extra pair of socks or a warm cup of tea may provide temporary relief, persistently cold hands and feet should not be brushed aside. Underlying health issues, including poor blood circulation, may sometimes be to blame.
Rather than relying on self-diagnosis, seek medical advice if your symptoms persist or are accompanied by other warning signs. Don’t get cold feet when it comes to your health.
3aea311825a5dc55: PARIS: Paris police issued an overnight curfew on Monday in two areas of the French capital, after a weekend marred by France’s worst rioting in years that targeted city halls, other public buildings and thousands of businesses across the country, the Associated Press (AP) reported.
The order aims to protect “people and property from the violence and looting,” the Paris police statement said.

The curfew prohibits anyone from entering or remaining on the Place de la Republique, where rioting took place Saturday, and the shopping neighbourhood of Les Halles, which has been subject to looting.
The curfew will be in effect from 11pm Monday until 6am Tuesday. In addition, gatherings and demonstrations are banned from 8pm, the Paris police said.
Earlier Monday, prime minister Sebastien Lecornu had called for “very limited” and “localised” curfews.

In northern France, local authorities imposed a curfew for children and teenagers under age 18 in several cities, including Lille, starting from Monday and for the next two days from 8pm to 6am. Nice, on the French Riviera, also imposed an overnight curfew for minors from 9pm.
Lecornu defended police handling of the unrest, saying that “despite scenes of severe violence and extensive property damage, no one was killed, and that is a miracle.”
He said that details of the curfews would be announced later Monday after consultations with mayors.
Mass protests in France are often tainted by violence on the fringes of otherwise peaceful marches, leading to clashes with police.

Saturday’s unrest recalled the riots that followed the fatal police shooting of a teenager in 2023, when authorities imposed local curfews, and violence during the yellow vest movement that began in 2018 over fuel prices and broader economic grievances.
The prime minister's instructions come after interior minister Laurent Nunez offered his resignation Sunday.
President Emmanuel Macron refused it “given the need for continued command of law enforcement in the current context,” Macron's office said in a statement Monday.
He instructed Nunez “to take all necessary steps to ensure full transparency about the failures in planning and intelligence-gathering that led to the violence,” the statement said.
Macron also asked for the introduction of “new policing tactics on the ground as quickly as possible” to put an end to the violence.
On Sunday evening, groups set fire to trash bins, bicycles and other objects in the streets and looted businesses in Paris, Lyon, Marseille and other cities.
That followed the violence during nationwide protests Saturday against rising living costs and poor conditions in schools. At least 2,400 people were arrested across the country.
Authorities estimated Monday that at least 3,000 businesses were damaged or looted in several cities.
In Marseille, the prefect banned any protest or other gatherings from noon to 8pm Monday.

“I submitted my resignation because I am responsible for everything that is happening,” Nunez said on France Inter radio. “Now the real issue is ensuring that this doesn’t happen again. … We obviously need to be better at anticipating the kind of mobilisation that is unfolding."
Nunez blamed the violence on “hordes of troublemakers and looters” and “far-left activists,” and said that police strategy needs to be adapted “in the face of extremely mobile groups.”
Authorities said that groups of hundreds of people sought confrontations with police and targeted public buildings, including city halls and other public offices.
Nunez acknowledged that authorities had “lost control” in some major cities on Saturday.
“You can’t look shopkeepers in the eye when hundreds of businesses have been looted and say we haven’t lost control in some of these major cities,” Nunez said.
Flames engulfed the 19th-century City Hall in Limoges, in central France, causing its roof to collapse and nearly destroying the building.
On Monday, cleanup crews and firefighters cleared shattered glass and other debris from the streets of Paris.
Ouri Zagoury, owner of a video game shop near Paris' Place de la Republique, said that he closed the store Saturday afternoon, but then saw looters forcing their way in on surveillance cameras.
“There were so many people coming in and out. And even though I called the police, they said not to intervene, that they would come, but they never did, which is another problem," Zagoury said.
Jordan Bardella, president of the far-right National Rally party, pointed to the government's failure to prevent violence.
“The government has failed, the head of state has failed in his essential duty of protecting the French people,” he told reporters at the party's headquarters.

“I call on the people of France now, beyond their right to protest, to use their voting power,” Bardella said. He is campaigning alongside far-right leader Marine Le Pen, whose polling numbers have suggested for months that she's the front-runner in next spring's presidential election.
9ffaaa9bc5c213a6: BOGOTA: 14 people were killed and 7 others injured following the collapse of an illegal gold mine in southwestern Colombia, local authorities said on Monday.
The accident took place in the rural Chambero sector of the Santa Barbara de Iscuande municipality, located in the province of Nariño.
Search and rescue operations have concluded, Nariño governor Luis Alfonso Escobar said.

The governor called on the national government, the national mining agency, and the ministry of mines and energy to accelerate the formalisation process for illegal and small-scale miners to improve working conditions and safety standards.
In August, 13 people died in a similar mining accident in the town of Policarpa, also in Nariño.
Informal and unregulated mining is common in rural parts of Colombia, where operations often lack adequate safety infrastructure, leading to frequent fatal accidents.

5896ab894451fee5: Over the Merdeka holidays, I went fishing with some friends off the Pahang and Johor coast. We started off from the Kuala Rompin jetties on a lovely morning with mist shrouding the mangrove and hovering over the river. It was a beautiful, peaceful sight.

Then the sun started getting hotter but the mist remained… and remained, acting in a most un-misty way. When we sailed away from the river mouth we could still see this “mist” all around us. It wasn’t mist. It was the haze, right there on the east coast hundreds of kilometres from the nearest Indonesian territories, yet enough of it was visible even in Pulau Tioman.

Over the last few months, I've been saying “I've never seen haze this bad, only to update it again multiple times on subsequent days. The haze last week was especially bad, but I’m sure as records go this too will be broken soon.

What can I say about the haze that hasn’t been said by many for years? I’m relatively healthy for my age and don’t have any bad allergy problems, but I still get headaches and nausea because of it. I can’t bear to think about what those with actual health issues must be going through.
The current haze seems worse than previous ones. It hangs heavy and feels thick and foul, often covering the sun and hills and gloomily blocking vision to barely a kilometre or so on the highway.

Everybody is frustrated with it, including an Indonesian official who slammed his Malaysian and Singaporean neighbours for complaining about the haze from Sumatra without acknowledging it also gives us oxygen during better days.

Hello! Our Indonesian official friend forgets his high school chemistry. Sumatra is passing us more than oxygen now, this time the said oxygen is all bound up with carbon and sulphur and nitrogen and other elements to form noxious and poisonous monoxides and dioxides and ozone!
Not exactly the kind of trade among friends. After decades of “importing” this stuff for months most years, we deserve a breather, if you’ll pardon the expression.
The Indonesians are also experimenting with clearing the haze with dry ice, which is supposed to lift the smoke particles higher into the atmosphere and clear the land.

Great – now the smoke particles will go even higher into the Indonesian skies to catch the stronger monsoon wind up there and even more of them can waft their way to Malaysia. Thank you again Indonesia!

In reality, Indonesia’s forest fire problem has gotten out of hand. The fires have literally gone underground, setting off the uncontrollable burning of dry underground peat. Once this catches fire, only the deluge of a monsoon can put it out.

This year a combination of factors, including a more severe El Nino, is exacerbating the problem; perhaps a madder-than-usual rush to burn forests, because there’s less of them left every year, is making things worse.

What we need to see is a more aggressive attitude among the political leaders of the region in fighting this menace. Our own leaders must also start demanding more be done by Indonesia to stop this perennial curse.

Of the culprits setting the forest on fire in Sumatra and Kalimantan are believed to include some big Malaysian plantation companies. If that is so, bring them to account and throw the book at them: I can guarantee there’ll be loud cheers from us ordinary Malaysians.
And ordinary Indonesians too. If it’s bad for us hundreds of kilometres away from the worst of it, just imagine how bad it must be for the unfortunate people living right there.

They can't go fishing away from the haze, like I did. They can’t get into private jets and fly out of the country to foreign clearer skies, as some people did. They just have to stay there and suck it all in literally and suffer now and/or die earlier later.

Our problems are not with the ordinary Indonesians, many of whom suffer even worse than us because of this haze. Our issues are with the Indonesian authorities who we don’t see treating the problem as the emergency it actually is.
And our issue is also with our own leaders who are more interested in maintaining peace and harmony while our people are literally choking with illness and maybe even death.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.
eee6ce4323556291: KUALA LUMPUR: When Muhammad Iqbal Mazlan woke up one morning in March 2023, everything had gone black.

The 37-year-old actor and director had been working on a documentary script the night before when he felt unusually tired and developed severe eye pain. He fell asleep expecting the discomfort to pass; instead, he woke to find that he could no longer see.
“I was actually in good health and had no unusual symptoms,” he recalled. “When I woke up, everything was pitch black. I had lost my sight.”

Iqbal said the cause was a condition called frosted branch angiitis linked to a cytomegalovirus infection: a diagnosis that brought an abrupt halt to a career he had spent years building across television, theatre and film.
“It was difficult to imagine what life would be like after that because the very gift I had relied on to earn a living was suddenly gone,” he said.

It took Iqbal more than a year to regain his footing physically. He underwent treatment for eye inflammation and later faced complications involving fluid in his lungs, which he said were linked to medication.
Returning to work proved even harder. Several production companies he had worked with before stopped responding when he offered his services as a director, host and voiceover artist.

“Many production companies had worked with me before and praised my work, but suddenly went silent when I fell ill,” he shared. “What hurt most was seeing people in the industry begin to distance themselves from me.”
One rejection in particular stayed with him: “We don’t have any confidence in you.”
To support himself, Iqbal now runs a food business in Shah Alam with a friend, selling buttermilk chicken rice and gulai kawah. But he did eventually find his way back onto a film set.
In June 2024, production company Art Ornament entrusted him with directing “Jay (Buka Langkah)”, which is expected to be released in January.
Directing without sight
Iqbal said losing his vision did not take away his ability to build a scene in his head. Instead, he relies more heavily on visualisation and detailed communication with the cinematographer.
“Even though I cannot see, I must have a clear visual in my mind to bring a script to life,” he said. “I imagine the scenes as though I am watching a film in a cinema.”

He then describes the framing, movement, sound and actor positioning as precisely as possible. “For instance, I will specify from which direction the actor should step forward, along with the accompanying sounds. Without visualisation, a director’s work would fall flat.”
Producer and co-director Aida Othman said Iqbal was given the role because of what he could still contribute creatively, while the crew supported him with the technical side of filming.
“We should not judge a person by what they lack, but by what they are capable of doing,” she said.

“Iqbal’s strength lies in his ability to explain clearly the characters, emotions and messages he wants to convey to the audience. We gave him the opportunity because we believed in his capabilities.”

Iqbal’s experience is not unique: Perkeso employment records from 2020 to 2026 show that of 716 visually impaired people placed in jobs across different sectors, only five entered arts, entertainment and recreation.
That figure does not explain why the number is so low, but it reflects how rare such placements remain.

Musician and composer Lui Chee Chau, 46, has faced similar difficulties. Visually impaired since infancy, he has formal music qualifications and more than a decade of industry experience, including work as a composer and sound engineer.

After losing a long-term job when the company he worked for closed, Lui began applying for music-related positions again. One interviewer praised his work but suggested he would be contacted only if there were tasks he could do from home.

Other applications went nowhere. Although no employer explicitly told him that his visual impairment was the reason, Lui believes assumptions about disability narrow the choices available before candidates are fully assessed.
“I believe this is one of the constraints we face when people limit our options based on their assumptions without assessing our actual abilities,” he said.
Lui now teaches piano and drums part-time and conducts a weekly music class at a local church.

For both men, the frustration is not simply about finding work; it is about being allowed to demonstrate what they can still do. Their careers may require different methods and more support than before, but neither talent nor experience disappeared with their sight.
b630c412b1a619a5: Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad bukan nama baharu dalam politik. Hampir dua dekad lalu, beliau muncul sebagai antara wajah muda PKR yang diberi peluang bertanding ketika perubahan politik mula berlaku di Selangor.
Pada 2008 ketika berusia 26 tahun, beliau memenangi DUN Seri Setia dengan majoriti 2,863 undi. Kemenangan itu menjadi permulaan kepada perjalanan agak pantas dalam politik negeri.

Beliau kemudian menjadi setiausaha politik kepada menteri besar Selangor ketika itu, Khalid Ibrahim. Selepas mempertahankan Seri Setia pada 2013, Nik Nazmi dilantik sebagai timbalan speaker DUN Selangor sebelum menyertai pentadbiran negeri sebagai exco dari 2014 hingga 2018.
Pada PRU14, Nik Nazmi mengambil keputusan meninggalkan Seri Setia dan mencuba nasib di peringkat Parlimen.

Setiawangsa ketika itu bukan pilihan mudah. Kerusi tersebut tidak pernah dimenangi pembangkang, tetapi Nik Nazmi berjaya menewaskan calon Barisan Nasional dan PAS dengan majoriti 14,372 undi. Empat tahun kemudian beliau mempertahankannya pada PRU15.

Kemenangan pada 2022 membawanya ke Jemaah Menteri apabila dilantik menerajui portfolio sumber asli dan alam sekitar. Dalam tempoh kira-kira 14 tahun, Nik Nazmi sudah bergerak daripada Adun muda kepada timbalan speaker, exco, Ahli Parlimen dan akhirnya menteri.
Laluan itu bagaimanapun tidak terus mendaki.

Pemilihan PKR tahun lalu menjadi titik perubahan penting. Nik Nazmi gagal mempertahankan jawatan naib presiden. Kekalahan itu disusuli keputusannya meletakkan jawatan sebagai menteri sumber asli dan kelestarian alam, yang menurutnya dibuat selepas tidak lagi mendapat mandat sebagai naib presiden parti.

Beberapa bulan kemudian, perubahan menjadi lebih besar. Nik Nazmi bersama Rafizi Ramli meninggalkan PKR dan mengosongkan kerusi Parlimen masing-masing sebelum mengambil alih Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama).
Dari situ, kedudukan politik Nik Nazmi berubah sama sekali. Beliau tidak lagi bergerak dalam parti mempunyai jentera, cawangan dan penyokong yang dibina selama puluhan tahun.
Bersama pula masih mencari tempat dalam gelanggang yang sudah sesak dengan BN, Pakatan Harapan (PH), Perikatan Nasional (PN) dan beberapa parti lebih kecil.
Itulah cabaran sebenar Nik Nazmi sekarang.
Namun, ketika beliau, Rafizi dan beberapa rakan perjuangan mulai rancak menyebarkan agenda Bersama terutama dalam berdepan PRN Melaka, bulan depan, Nik Nazmi berdepan satu lagi cabaran hebat.
Kontroversi tambah tekanan

Kontroversi terbaru membabitkan penahanannya oleh Jabatan Agama Islam Selangor atas dakwaan khalwat menambah satu lagi perkara yang perlu diuruskan, tetapi ia bukan keseluruhan cerita politik Nik Nazmi.

Beliau mengesahkan penahanan itu, memohon maaf kepada isteri, keluarga dan Bersama atas apa yang disifatkannya sebagai ‘kesilapan pertimbangan’, sambil menegaskan tiada perbuatan sumbang berlaku. Kes itu masih melalui proses undang-undang.
Bersama kemudian memutuskan merehatkannya daripada semua aktiviti rasmi parti selama tiga bulan, bermula 20 Okt (hari ini) hingga 19 Jan 2027.
Bagi seorang tokoh politik berpengalaman, kontroversi boleh reda. Yang lebih sukar ialah memulihkan momentum apabila ia berlaku ketika parti sedang cuba memperkenalkan dirinya kepada pengundi.
Nik Nazmi kini berada di persimpangan yang mungkin tidak pernah dibayangkannya ketika kali pertama memenangi Seri Setia 18 tahun lalu.
Dahulu, setiap langkahnya membawa kepada tanggungjawab lebih besar — dari DUN ke Parlimen, kemudian ke Kabinet. Kini beliau perlu bermula daripada kedudukan yang jauh kurang selesa.

Jawatan menteri sudah dilepaskan. PKR sudah ditinggalkan. Kerusi Parlimen juga dikosongkan. Parti baharunya pula belum membuktikan kemampuan memenangi kerusi, selain perlu menyelesaikan kontroversi peribadi.
Sebab itu, PRU16 bukan sekadar peluang untuk Nik Nazmi kembali ke Parlimen. Ia akan menunjukkan sama ada pengalaman dan nama yang dibinanya sejak 2008 masih mempunyai daya tarikan.
Barangkali bagi Nik Nazmi, itu cabaran politik paling besar sepanjang kerjayanya.

5383733737c3d614: BOGOTA: Ahead of an election that could return the right to power in Brazil, polls show support slipping for recently elected conservative leaders across Latin America.

New surveys in Peru, Colombia, Chile and Argentina suggest voters are losing patience with governments elected on promises to curb crime, revive weak economies and forge closer ties with US president Donald Trump.
Peru's conservative president Keiko Fujimori and her hardline, gun-toting Colombian counterpart, Abelardo de la Espriella, are the latest newcomers to see their ratings fall.
An Ipsos poll last week showed approval of Fujimori dropping to 40% from 57% when she took office in August, while De la Espriella's fell more than three points in his first month in office.

In Chile, where voters elected their most conservative president in three decades last year amid concerns over organised crime, one-quarter of president Jose Antonio Kast's supporters say they regret backing him, according to the left-wing Fundacion Nodo XXI.
Argentine president Javier Milei, a hero to free-market conservatives across the region, has also seen his ratings hit record lows a year before seeking re-election.

"I think a lot of these governments raised expectations probably unrealistically. People want quick results, which are impossible to produce," Michael Shifter, senior fellow at The Inter-American Dialogue think tank in Washington, told AFP.
But the backlash has little to do with ideology, he cautioned.
"I'm not sure that if these were governments of the left that it would be any different," he said.

An AmericasBarometer survey of more than 25,000 people in 21 countries found weak support for the leaders of eight US allies that belong to Trump's "Shield of the Americas" alliance: Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, the Dominican Republic, Ecuador, Guatemala, Panama and Paraguay.
'Concrete action'
Nowhere is impatience for better governance more visible than in Bolivia, where voters dumped the long-ruling socialists in the midst of the country's worst economic crisis in 40 years.
President Rodrigo Paz was elected as a moderate, pro-business alternative, but was only six months into his mandate when demonstrators demanding his resignation blockaded major cities.
Many blame the 59-year-old for failing to end crippling fuel shortages.
"I thought it would be different, that things were going to change," Jamil Alanoca, a 19-year-old business student, told AFP.
Across the border in Peru, voters went to the polls in April and June seeking relief from an extortion epidemic and are already showing frustration at the lack of results.
"A problem that has persisted for so many years (insecurity) isn't going to be solved overnight," Guillermo Loli, director of opinion polls at Ipsos Peru, told AFP.
But "at least concrete actions should be seen," he said.
The Bukele exception
Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's iron-fisted approach to his country's gangs has earned him a cult-like following.
The self-described "world's coolest dictator" enjoys approval of 83%, according to the AmericasBarometer survey, after driving crime rates to historic lows through a sweeping anti-gang crackdown.
The gains were achieved by jailing more than 90,000 suspects under a four-year-old state of emergency that rights groups say has been marked by serious abuses.

"Bukele's El Salvador remains a defining experiment - a state that traded liberties for safety and, by these measures, delivered greater safety," the 2026 Pulse of Democracy report produced by Vanderbilt University using AmericasBarometer polling said.
Shifter expressed doubt that Bukele's success against domestic gangs could be replicated against the transnational crime networks operating elsewhere in the region.
"Bukele, I think, is really sui generis, he's the exception," he said.
Chilean pensioner Leoncio Silva said he believed that, given more time, Kast would vanquish the foreign gangs blamed for a surge in violence in his country.
"Let's wait a year and see," he urged.

7c920984942db02c: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 20 — For delivery riders in Johor, escaping the thick haze that has settled over the state is not as simple as staying indoors. Their livelihoods depend on being out on the road, even as the polluted air takes a toll on their health.

As air quality reached very unhealthy levels in several parts of the state last week, riders reported sore throats, stinging eyes and other symptoms, leaving some to weigh the cost of fewer deliveries against the risks of prolonged exposure.

The haze, carried across the region by smoke from fires in Indonesia, has prompted Johor to extend school and educational institution closures until October 23, even as outdoor workers continue their daily routines.
For Ghani Jaafar, a 50-year-old food and beverage delivery rider on the outskirts of Johor Bahru, the effects of the haze were difficult to ignore.
After spending long hours making deliveries on his motorcycle, he developed a sore throat and mild nasal irritation.
“The symptoms happened early last week and persisted up till the weekend.
“If the haze becomes severe this week, I will consider temporarily scaling down on my deliveries,” he told Malay Mail while making his rounds yesterday.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Delivery rider Ghani Jaafar, 50, said he experienced a sore throat and nasal irritation after prolonged exposure to the haze in Johor last week. — Picture by Ben Tan
But cutting back on work is hardly straightforward.
Ghani also works part-time as a construction site supervisor, leaving him with little opportunity to escape the outdoor conditions. Between the two jobs, he spends more than 10 hours a day working.
“It is meaningless for people like me to be indoors as both my jobs are based outdoors. On average, I spend more than 10 hours a day doing both jobs.
“The best I can do is to drink more water, monitor the current Air Pollutant Index (API) and try to minimise being outdoors,” he said.
He is aware of the risks, from coughing and eye irritation to sore throats and shortness of breath. Yet avoiding the haze would also mean giving up working hours.
Prolonged exposure to haze, particularly fine particulate matter known as PM2.5, can irritate the eyes and respiratory tract and aggravate existing conditions such as asthma.

In an October 15 advisory, the Health Ministry urged the public to avoid outdoor activities when the API exceeds 100, the threshold for unhealthy air quality, and recommended N95 masks for those who must venture outside. Employers were also advised to provide the masks to outdoor workers.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Part-time delivery rider Mohd Eddin Sanusi, 38, called on the government to provide financial assistance to gig workers affected by the haze in Johor. — Picture by Ben Tan
For Mohd Eddin Sanusi, another delivery rider, the problem has been particularly acute on the road.
The 38-year-old said the haze had left his eyes sore and stinging, sometimes affecting his ability to see clearly while riding his motorcycle.
“Since early last week, I have had sore eyes that started with a stinging sensation from the haze.
“This also affected my vision when I’m riding my motorcycle,” he told Malay Mail when met at a 24-hour restaurant here recently.
“I wash my face more often and use eye drops to relieve the soreness.
“Besides that, I was advised by my family to avoid any delivery runs if the API is above 200,” said Mohd Eddin, who also works as a car rental executive in Pontian.
Under Malaysia’s API classification, readings between 201 and 300 are considered very unhealthy, while those above 300 are classified as hazardous.

Johor recorded 30,648 cases of asthma and upper respiratory tract infections in October as of mid-month, a 20.7 per cent week-on-week increase, according to state Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali.
Mohd Eddin began making deliveries three years ago to supplement his income. He described the latest haze as the worst he had encountered since taking up the work.
“This time round, the haze has hit most of southern Johor, where most delivery riders are based.
“It would be good if the government could come out with an assistance package for gig workers like me who are affected by the haze,” he said.
For some riders, the trade-off is already reshaping their working routines.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Delivery rider Putera Mohammad Aidil, 41 (3rd left), has turned to an air quality monitoring app to track haze conditions and plan his daily deliveries in Johor. — Picture courtesy of Putera Mohammad Aidil
Putera Mohammad Aidil, 41, who makes food deliveries for his family’s stall in Bandar Baru Uda, has begun limiting how far he travels after experiencing a sore throat and eye irritation.
The Johor Bahru-based rider said he was concerned about the long-term consequences of breathing polluted air while working.
He recently downloaded an air quality monitoring app to help plan his daily deliveries, but it was advice from his wife that led him to restrict his routes to nearby residential areas.
“My family operates a food stall in Bandar Baru Uda and I normally do the motorcycle deliveries,” he said when contacted yesterday.
“With the current haze and due to health concerns, my wife told me to concentrate my deliveries within the nearby residential area only.
“In a way, this cuts down on my deliveries and contact with the haze, but it also affects my business as well.
“However, as a family man with three young children, I can’t forgo my health.”
f58a6e69d405a131: SAN ANTONIO, Oct 20 — After more than three decades of Republican dominance, Democrats in Texas see a rare chance to break through in November’s midterm elections, as voter anger over immigration raids and the cost-of-living tests US President Donald Trump’s support.
No Democrat has won statewide office in the conservative southern state since 1994, and Trump carried Texas by nearly 14 percentage points in the 2024 presidential election.
But with a US Senate seat and the governorship at stake on November 3, recent polls suggest Republicans face an unusually competitive challenge.

At the forefront is James Talarico, a 37-year-old former teacher and state lawmaker whose blend of Christian faith, economic populism and appeals for political unity has helped make the Senate race one of the country’s most closely watched.

A University of Texas poll released this week put Talarico ahead of Republican Ken Paxton, the state’s attorney general and a staunch Trump ally, by 50 per cent to 47 per cent — a lead within the survey’s margin of error.
A separate UMass Lowell poll found the two candidates tied.

A Presbyterian seminarian, Talarico has sought to attract independents and Republicans disillusioned with Trump, arguing that Texans have more in common than the country’s increasingly bitter political divisions suggest.
“I’ll always put Texas before any political party,” he has said.
Trump, however, has campaigned aggressively for Paxton, warning at a recent rally in San Antonio that losing the seat could jeopardise the Republicans’ narrow Senate majority.

“It’s a killer in Congress because we have a very close majority. We can’t let that happen,” Trump said, mocking Talarico with the nickname “Talafreako” and accusing Democrats of wanting to reopen the country’s borders.
Paxton’s baggage

Trump backed Paxton over incumbent Senator John Cornyn in a bitter Republican primary battle, despite warnings that the attorney general’s history of controversy could imperil the party’s hold on the seat.
Paxton was impeached by the Republican-controlled Texas House in 2023 over allegations of corruption and abuse of power, although the state Senate subsequently acquitted him.
In an extraordinary twist, Dan Cogdell, one of the lawyers who defended Paxton during the proceedings, has since endorsed Talarico.
More recently, The Wall Street Journal reported that Paxton spent New Year’s Eve in Dubai with two American businessmen indicted over alleged healthcare fraud. Both have pleaded not guilty.
Yet Paxton retains support among Trump-aligned conservatives, including some who acknowledge misgivings about their candidate.
“I’ll be honest, I don’t think he’s the best representation, but he’s the best one we are being offered right now,” Mark Aponte, 58, told AFP at Trump’s San Antonio rally.
He said he considered Paxton the best available choice to protect his priorities, including public safety and Christian rights.
Cracks in Trump’s coalition
Beyond Paxton’s personal controversies, Democrats are looking to exploit growing discontent over immigration enforcement and the economy.
Trump’s commanding victory in Texas in 2024 owed partly to substantial gains among Latino voters, particularly along the state’s southern border with Mexico.
But some of those voters are now reconsidering their support.
Benny Melendez, a construction business owner and the son of immigrants, voted for Trump but says the administration’s immigration crackdown has devastated his business.
“My work, my profits and my workforce have all been cut in half,” he told AFP, adding that he was deeply troubled by the fear and family separations caused by immigration enforcement.

Cattle industry groups in Texas, Kansas and Oklahoma have also warned that immigration raids are disrupting agricultural businesses, deterring legally employed workers and threatening to drive up beef prices.
A May survey by the Latino civil rights group UnidosUS found that one in five Texas Latino voters who backed Trump in 2024 would not do so again if given another chance.

The broader discontent has also given Democrats hope in the race for governor, where three-term Republican incumbent Greg Abbott faces an unexpectedly close contest against state lawmaker Gina Hinojosa.
Hinojosa has focused her campaign on the cost of living, seeking to appeal to voters beyond the traditional Democratic base.
For Melendez, disillusionment with Trump has become reason enough to switch sides.
“I didn’t vote for Trump because I liked him,” he told AFP. “I voted for Trump to punish Biden. And I’m going to vote for the Democrat for the same reason: to punish Trump.” — AFP
c184b13c6a8e6ed0: WASHINGTON, Oct 20 — Britain’s Met Office says this year’s El Nino is “unprecedented.” Japan’s weather agency has called it the strongest ever observed. US forecasters say it still trails the biggest events in its record books.
How can they all be right?
The answer lies in how they measure El Nino’s strength, with meteorological agencies using different methods to assess the climate phenomenon that make direct comparisons difficult.

“By any measure, we are looking at a very strong El Nino,” climate scientist Emily Becker of the University of Miami told AFP, adding that only once it is over will scientists be able to assess how big it is and “where it fits in the context of history.”
Natural climate driver

The Pacific Ocean’s El Nino Southern Oscillation (ENSO) is the planet’s main natural climate driver. Normally, trade winds blow east to west along the equator, pushing warm water from South America toward Asia, while cold water rises from the depths to replace it.
El Ninos, which occur every two to seven years on average and last nine to 12 months, disrupt this pattern.

The trade winds weaken and warm water is pushed back east toward the Americas. That shift in where ocean heat is released into the atmosphere ripples across global weather, making some regions cooler and wetter and others hotter and drier.
In describing the El Nino as unprecedented, the Met Office points to raw temperatures in the Pacific.
“Our observations confirm that sea-surface temperatures in the central equatorial Pacific have now surpassed levels recorded during previous El Nino events,” it said in a statement to AFP.
But absolute temperatures are just one way of measuring El Nino’s strength. Agencies also look at anomalies — how far temperatures rise above a historic baseline — to assess the event.

The Japan Meteorological Agency last week declared this El Nino the strongest on record based on how far sea surface temperatures were above normal in the Nino3 region of the eastern Pacific. By its count, the event beat 1997 in observations going back to 1949.
The US watches a neighboring box, Nino3.4, in the east-central Pacific.

It declares an El Nino when temperatures there run at least 0.5C above normal and the atmosphere responds, weakening the trade winds and shifting tropical rainfall eastward. This process is known as “ocean-atmosphere coupling.”
Accounting for climate change
How “normal” is defined has been a matter of significant debate.

The US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) and other agencies including the UN’s World Meteorological Organization long used the Oceanic Nino Index (ONI), which compares temperatures to a 30-year average that is updated every five years, so that the baseline keeps pace with a warming climate.
But with climate change speeding up and warming oceans worldwide, NOAA now uses the Relative Oceanic Nino Index (RONI), and the WMO is in the process of switching.

RONI also relies on a 30-year average but goes on to measure how warm or cool the east-central Pacific is compared to the rest of the tropical ocean, because it is that difference that drives the weather impacts we care about.

“We were finding a mismatch between the temperature of the tropical Pacific and the impacts,” said Becker about the old index. La Nina years, when the central and eastern tropical Pacific is cooler than normal, were producing stronger effects than their rating suggested, and El Ninos weaker ones.

NOAA projects this El Nino will be the strongest in its records, which go back to 1950, if the three-month average RONI anomaly reaches 2.5°C or higher, a level that would put it above the 1982-83, 2015-16, and 1997-98 events.
The chances are rated “high,” but not yet certain.

“Regardless of where we’re ranking or how we’re measuring this event, it’s an incredible opportunity to study and understand this very powerful phenomenon in the context of a warming world,” said Becker. — AFP
53f000ee17f75c95: PETALING JAYA: A public spat between DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng and Penang DAP chief Steven Sim is likely to become more pronounced "but will not boil over" before the succession of Penang’s chief minister is decided, says a political analyst.

James Chin of the University of Tasmania said tensions between the two longstanding party rivals are expected to persist as the question of political succession gains prominence, with Sim among the leading candidates to become the next chief minister.
“The fight will become more pronounced before the new chief minister is announced,” Chin said. However, the dispute was unlikely to reach boiling point as no party election was imminent.

Lim singled out SME Corp Malaysia chairman Teng Chang Khim, accusing him of focusing on criticising DAP leaders rather than addressing issues affecting SMEs. Lim said Sim was entitled to disagree with him but should not allow such attacks to continue.

Earlier last week, Lim had criticised the government’s decision to extend the RM2,000 minimum wage to existing foreign workers and require employers and foreign employees to contribute 2% each to the EPF. He said the measures would raise costs for small and medium enterprises.

Two weeks ago, Sim, who is minister of entrepreneur development and cooperatives, had said the government had agreed to exempt smaller enterprises from further increases in minimum wage for the time being.
Universiti Malaya socio-political analyst Awang Azman Pawi said Lim might be seeking to reassert his influence within DAP, although his motives were unclear.

He said Lim’s experience as the party’s adviser and former secretary-general remained an asset, but political influence increasingly depended on delivering practical policy solutions rather than seniority alone.
Awang Azman said Sim, as a serving minister, should demonstrate leadership through concrete results rather than through public confrontation.

He warned that personal attacks could undermine both leaders’ credibility and distract from substantive policy concerns. Allegations involving Sim’s associates should not automatically be attributed to the minister himself, he added.
“The public generally expects ministers to concentrate on governance, economic challenges and policy delivery rather than becoming embroiled in prolonged internal disputes,” he said.

Awang Azman said Lim’s criticism would carry greater weight if supported by economic evidence and practical alternatives, while Sim could show political maturity by addressing the policy concerns without personalising the dispute.

e5eadce826998ef4: To feed its Indiana datacenters with plenty of juice, Amazon is funding the development of a new nuclear facility that will provide nearly 1 gigawatt of power. However, we'll have to see if this happens anytime soon, given the immature technology it's using.

Amazon said on Monday that it was funding the project with an undisclosed amount of cash as part of an expansion of its existing deal with X-energy, a next-generation nuclear power startup focusing on building small modular reactors (SMRs) powered by Tri-Structural ISOtropic (TRISO) fuel pellets and cooled by helium gas.
Amazon would tell us only that it’s “investing billions in nuclear energy projects” without getting specific on this project.

According to X-energy, the project will see Amazon fund the development of 12 of those SMRs, its Xe-100 model, in Sullivan County, Indiana, at the site of a former coal power plant. Once up and running, the facility will supply 960 megawatts of grid-connected electricity, with Amazon contracting as the first power purchaser from the future plant.

As for when it might come online, that’s anyone’s guess. Amazon wouldn’t tell us, only pointing us to an article in Indiana newspaper the South Bend Tribune in which an X-energy representative said it could be completed “as early as the mid-2030s,” though “the timeline could change the further the project gets developed.”
That’s quite likely given X-energy’s current status and the state of next-generation nuclear power more generally, and to understand why it helps to understand how nuclear permitting works in the US.

First off, despite the promises, hype, and mountains of cash poured into nuclear power by the tech industry, the US has yet to build a single operable SMR. China and Russia have built functional SMRs. A single experimental unit has achieved criticality in the US, but it’s not a functional, power-producing reactor and was only built to demonstrate the ability for a specific design to become one. The company with that experimental US SMR is not X-energy, who has yet to build a working reactor.

As to how reactors get approved in the US, there are two pathways that nuclear power companies can pursue: One is to get a standard design approval from the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC). That pathway gives a company license to build a reactor of a specific model wherever they want, as the design has been deemed safe independent of any physical site. That means the certified reactor can be sold and built without the need for the NRC to recertify the core design each time a project gets underway.

There is only one company in the US that has a standard design approval for an SMR: Nuscale, which has yet to build a single reactor, has no projects under construction, and has already abandoned a Utah plant due to lack of interest from power distributors.

The other option allows SMR developers to get approval for a site-specific project, which is quicker and involves the NRC blessing a particular reactor in a particular place. There have been several of those permits awarded, with Kairos Power being approved to build an SMR in Oak Ridge, Tennessee in partnership with Google, General Electric planning another SMR in Oak Ridge, and TerraPower inching forward with its own project in Wyoming despite delays.

Notice X-energy isn’t mentioned there, either. The company claims that it’s in “the final phases” of NRC approval for a construction permit in Texas, where it’ll supply power for a Dow Chemical manufacturing plant, but that likely won’t matter too much for the Indiana project’s timeline. As mentioned above, nuclear construction permits are site specific, and the Texas plant only involves four reactors - far fewer than the 12 planned in Indiana.
X-energy didn’t respond to questions for this story, but Amazon told us it's not going to be involved in any way with getting approval across the finish line for the Indiana plant.

“Amazon's role is as an investor … as well as committing to being the first customer for power produced from the facility,” a company spokesperson told us. “New technologies like this often need initial customers to help de-risk projects and provide funding so they can be built and scaled to commercial availability, and that is the role Amazon is playing by helping to fund the project's development.”
Like other large, ambitious next-generation nuclear projects, in other words, this one is just as much in the maybe column as the rest. ®

3bf87038d3406f87: It may not be enough to just use LLMs to write your code when you can also use them to adjust it while your program runs. DoubleAI, a Tel Aviv, Israel-based startup founded in 2023, on Monday introduced Maxwell, a code execution model (CEM) that evaluates, optimizes, and rewrites binary code during execution.

Named for Maxwell's Demon, a creature imagined by physicist and mathematician James Clerk Maxwell in 1867 as part of a thought experiment on entropy, the Maxwell CEM preprocesses algorithms and machine instructions to maximize performance on available hardware.
Maxwell is similar in concept to a just-in-time compiler, but provides more flexibility and formally verifies the equivalence of replacement code. Source code isn't touched.

"Both Maxwell and a JIT compiler work while the program runs and both produce new machine code," said doubleAI co-founder Gal Beniamini, who holds a PhD in theoretical computer science, in an email to The Register. "The difference is that a compiler can't do high-level reasoning. It can't, for example, change the algorithm. Maxwell can and does.

"One of the reasons why JIT compilers are so narrow is that, even though they can be data-dependent, the changes they make must be deterministic and correct 'by construction,' since JIT compilers are 'unthinking' classical algorithms.

"Maxwell brings the expressive power of frontier AI into the 'JIT' setting. In addition, Maxwell relies on formal verification to write actual, hard proofs that show that its optimizations are sound. This expands the scope of its allowed optimisation far beyond that of any algorithm or compiler."
Beniamini pointed to sorting as an example. The compiler, he said, will make a general-purpose sorting algorithm run as fast as it can, but it won't swap it out for a different algorithm.
Compilers, said Beniamini, make decisions before the program runs and have to be narrow and conservative in their choices.
Maxwell, he said, works with more information, isn't just a one-pass operation, and operates at a higher level.

"It sees the exact hardware the program has landed on, and the actual shapes and types of the data flowing through it (information that is only available during runtime!)," Beniamini explained. "It also sees the state of the environment, what else is running in the same program, and which actual bottlenecks express themselves, and under which conditions. This allows it to specialize in ways a compiler never can."
Since Maxwell operates continuously, it can keep improving programs as new bottlenecks arise. And it can "reason" in a way that compilers cannot.
Maxwell's approach wouldn't be possible if the model rewrote code in a way that introduced errors on the fly, so the formal proof capability is not optional.
According to doubleAI, Maxwell has made data pipelines more than 38x faster and AI inference kernels more than 4.5x faster.

LTX-2.5, an open world model that generates 4K video, managed to do so almost twice as fast with the help of Maxwell. Maxwell's optimizations reduced the data being exchanged between GPUs and optimized the kernel selection to drop unnecessary token padding.
Maxwell's optimization capability varies depending on the source code and the hardware.

"Maxwell does best on code that is algorithmic, and which can be tailored to hardware in a non-trivial manner," said Beniamini. "That being said, even code that isn't like that, but is written in a high level language like Python, can usually enjoy far reaching optimisations due to the available overhang. The same is true for PyTorch graphs, which (even under Torch's compiler) tend to be extremely far from optimal."
It can also help with code security. Beniamini said Maxwell can eliminate issues like memory errors by proving their non-existence as part of the formalization process.
"Anecdotally, we have found such issues in Python itself, through the use of Maxwell – i.e., cases in which Python was not memory safe, and where Maxwell proved that to be the case," he said.
And better still, Maxwell's tracing and profiling don't incur much if any overhead on either the CPU or GPU.

"The maximal overhead of Maxwell's tracing and profiling is 2 percent (when it isn't tracing, that falls to zero, of course), and the optimisations that Maxwell yields far outweigh that," said Beniamini. "We also apply Maxwell to the runtime itself, so that we get back a much larger than 2 percent 'flat' speedup, across the board. So in short: it's never slower."

The installation process is similarly light-touch: Devs install the runtime and run their code, with the Maxwell model hosted by doubleAI. This arrangement, however, does require some amount of trust.

Amnon Shashua, co-founder and CEO of doubleAI, founder and departing CEO of Mobileye and a professor of computer science at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, said in a statement that AI has changed how software is written and now is changing how it runs.

"CEMs, and Maxwell in particular, are agents on behalf of the hardware as opposed to code agents that are on behalf of the human user," he said. "In other words, they are the first AI that works for the machine, not the programmer." ®
